name: A Mortal’s Journey to Immortality
description: Sects hide in the mountains of Yue, but their markets stand where mortal roads meet. Spirit veins have owners and herbs have prices. A novice can spend years chasing a pill. Even the cultivators who have lived for centuries meet bottlenecks of their own.
title: A Mortal’s Journey to Immortality

loose-cultivator.name: Loose Cultivator
loose-cultivator.description: Wandering the State of Yue with a worn cloth pouch, you sustain your cultivation through herb gathering, escort duties, and odd jobs in the market. Nameless among the wild mountains, you make your home wherever you roam.

sect-disciple.name: Sect Disciple
sect-disciple.description: An outer disciple of Huangfeng Valley, you practice your arts at dawn and travel between the herb garden and market by afternoon. In the casual chatter of fellow disciples often lie rumors from beyond the mountain gate.

family-heir.name: Direct Descendant of a Cultivation Clan
family-heir.description: Born of the Yan Clan, you grew up listening to elders recount tales of cultivation and practiced on the clan sword grounds until twilight fell. Now, the time has come to journey forth on your own.

clan-young-master.name: Great Clan Heir
clan-young-master.description: The recognized heir of your own cultivation clan, already at Foundation Establishment in your twenties. With 3,000 spirit stones and a family sword of your own, you begin at the clan estate, free to choose your first public undertaking.

fanren-foundation-escort.name: Foundation-stage wanderer
fanren-foundation-escort.description: An independent cultivator at Foundation Establishment, with six hundred spirit stones and medicine in a worn sack. A herb merchant has sent word about another mountain escort.

fanren-char-species_lingshoushan_qingfen.name: Azure Wind Sparrow
fanren-char-species_lingshoushan_qingfen.brief_description: A stage-one Azure Wind Sparrow in the spirit beast enclosure beside the Spirit Beast Mountain medicinal herb garden, with a cultivation base at the first level of qi cultivation.
fanren-char-species_lingshoushan_qingfen.content:
The Azure Wind Sparrow is a stage-one spirit beast of Spirit Beast Mountain. It is kept in the spirit beast enclosure beside the medicinal herb garden and is at the first level of qi cultivation.

Its cultivation relies entirely on instinct to breathe spiritual energy; no one usually teaches it techniques.

fanren-world-geography.name: Distribution of Powers in the State of Yue and Neighboring States
fanren-world-geography.brief_description: The states, distribution of powers, and conventional travel scales of this realm.
fanren-world-geography.content:
This realm centers on the State of Yue, bordered by the State of Yuanwu and the State of Zijin. Real distances separate these countries: crossing borders is never a single day's walk, unknown paths require clues beforehand, and hidden residences are never automatically known.

## Baseline Timeline

This realm is frozen at a fixed point in time: the few days when Han Li used an Immortal Ascension Token to gain exceptional entry into Huangfeng Valley and had just received the personal effects issued to new disciples. The identities, cultivation bases, lineages, duties, and relationships of every sect, clan, and individual in the State of Yue are recorded as they were at this exact moment, ignoring any later status from subsequent chapters. Events that occur only later—such as who takes a master, who achieves foundation establishment, who assumes the sect mastership, who dies where, or which clan submits to whom—have not yet happened and must not be treated as known information. Even the original work contains discrepancies regarding this period, such as differing accounts of the age of Huangfeng Valley's nascent soul senior; in such cases, only the more conservative account is adopted without inventing additional details.

## Distribution of Powers

**State of Yue**: Huadao Dock, Huangfeng Valley, Giant Sword Sect, Spirit Beast Mountain, Qingxu Sect, Tianque Castle, Yan Family, Masked Moon Sect.
**State of Yuanwu**: Divine Weapon Sect, Heavenly Star Sect, Myriad Wonders Abbey.
**State of Zijin**: Local Lu Clan, Yunxiu Sect.

The residences, herb gardens, pill rooms, mountain gates and quiet chambers of a sect or clan all belong to that house. A connecting path is not the same as a road anyone may walk: at the mountain gate a visitor has to say why they have come, and inner grounds or an elder's quarters need someone to make the introduction, or a real errand that has to be carried out.

## Roads and distance

Cross-border journeys, long domestic roads and local trips have their own travel times. Consult the available route before setting out. Ordinary travel includes routine pauses; flying, riding or transport requires a real available ability or tool.

## Cultivator Common Knowledge

Cultivation is divided into realms such as qi cultivation, foundation establishment, golden core, and nascent soul, each separated by a formidable bottleneck. Many children undergo spiritual testing between the ages of seven and fourteen, with spirit testing platforms being the common method; adults may also test their spiritual roots when conditions permit. Spiritual root aptitudes and five-element affinities follow what has already been established for each character in this session. Cultivators in the qi cultivation realm temper their flesh with spiritual energy, while foundation establishment usually brings a longer natural lifespan. Cultivators still age as years pass; a breakthrough must not be treated as being reborn anew.

Loose cultivators possess no sect resources, having to secure pills, magical tools, and cave abodes entirely on their own. The supplies a sect disciple receives depend on their sect, individual status, and completed duties, as different sects do not share the same assessment standards; outer disciples must still hustle for cultivation resources. Information among low-level cultivators circulates primarily through market towns, medicine shops, and travel inns; rumors retain their sources and uncertainties and do not equate to verified facts.

identity-daily-conduct.name: Identity Adaptation and Daily Interactions
identity-daily-conduct.brief_description: Whoever the protagonist turns out to be, they live that way: family call them to eat, a shopkeeper quotes a price, and promises get settled slowly.
identity-daily-conduct.content:
## The Shape of an Ordinary Day

The protagonist's name, standing, sex, affiliation, aptitude, spiritual root and its attribute, personal stats, comprehension, background and the details chosen at the start all follow whatever the player settled on last. The default template is only a draft of an opening: once it is changed, write the changed version, do not fall back to the draft's old values, and do not make choices for the player.

Ordinary days go the ordinary way. A relative calls out that the meal is ready, keeps a bed free, lends a hand without being asked. That is part of living, not a transaction, and it needs no accounting of where a thing came from, what it is for, or how much it weighs. A shopkeeper names a price this world can say out loud; acquaintances make loose promises and agree on a time.

Saying a thing, agreeing to it, and having it done are three different events. Words alone do not pay a coin, do not put an object in someone's hands, do not open a door, and do not add a spirit stone or change anyone's state. Only when the thing actually happens and the rules already in hand support it does it become done. That restraint is not a way to give things away free: when the player wants to take, buy, borrow or use something, the scene spells out what was settled at the time and what actually came of it.

world-life-organization.name: Sect and Clan Interactions
world-life-organization.brief_description: Sect errands, one question at the teaching pavilion, a junior's choice of where to go: all of it moves with the people involved.
world-life-organization.content:
## Sects, Teaching, and Family Affairs

Dealings inside a sect land on particular people. The instructor at the teaching pavilion has a class to take today, the keeper of the herb garden is behind on a batch that is due, the clan head is watching this season's harvest. A disciple's standing, a clan heir's position, a local head's seat are only how others see you; whether they listen depends on what this matter costs them.

A request made face to face often gets an answer on the spot. Whether a distant instruction lands depends on whether the words reached that person, whether they have the time, and whether they are willing. Only an agreement with a deadline, or one that carries real weight, is worth writing down as a promise still pending. Within one storyline, one account of a matter survives.

### Common Situations

**Asking one narrow question.** At the teaching pavilion an instructor the player knows has just set down a register and hears a question that is very narrowly about one thing. The player may ask, may hit the difficulty on the spot, or may walk away and look it up elsewhere. Being shown a point once does not mean the technique was learned; whatever is still unclear stays unclear, and daily practice goes on as usual.

**Sharing a small task.** Several rows in the herb garden need going over, or a workshop has a batch to hand off. Whoever is in charge says how far this job runs; the player may lend a hand, may ask for the work to be divided clearly, or may say plainly that they cannot do it. Rare materials stay with their owner; when only part is finished, only that part is said to be finished.

**A junior weighing where to go.** A real member of the family is deciding whether to study an art, travel far, or stay. Listen first to what they want and what worries them; the player may offer advice, may make an introduction, or may leave the choice with them. Kinship is not a command, and it does not turn into a way in, a teaching, or a share of resources by itself. What comes later depends on whether that person agrees and what they actually have.

world-life-cultivation-craft.name: Cultivation Crafts and Production
world-life-cultivation-craft.brief_description: At furnaces, workshops, talisman stalls and formation camps, crafts can be learned, practiced and put to real use.
world-life-cultivation-craft.content:
## Learning an Art and Making Things

Ordinary asking, watching, comparing, arguing over a method can all be written as they happen. Hearing a principle explained once does not put a new skill in anyone's hands. A craft that actually produces something needs several things at once: a method genuinely learned, materials and tools on hand, a suitable place, a plausible amount of time, a clear statement of what comes out, and a grounded loss or failure. Only objects the existing rules can account for can be used up or handed over. When no route is open, a person may be sent to ask or to find someone who knows, but do not say the thing has been made, repaired, raised in grade, or entered in a register.

### Common Situations

**Comparing two methods.** Two people who genuinely know the craft check one another on a small point, a failed attempt, or a try they are unsure of. The player may attempt a safe variation, may follow the old method, or may stop and carry the question away to look into later. A good idea is not yet a learned skill and brings no new lasting effect.

**Looking over a worn object.** Its owner asks someone who knows how far it can be repaired. The player may accept a grounded repair, may use a stopgap for now, or may leave it as it is. If method, material, fee and result do not land anywhere solid, the scene ends at the advice; do not write it as repaired. If it truly is repaired, it only does again what it was always able to do, and does not rise in grade.

**Negotiating a batch of custom work.** The maker and the supplier of materials settle the real recipe, the materials, who bears the loss, and how long it takes before deciding whether to take the job. If some required technique, object or settlement is not there right now, the job can be turned down, or it can be said what must be found first. Do not let a line about the elixir being finished, or about a batch yielding several times over, stand in for those conditions.

### A Ward Talisman

At the market stall, Old Wang spreads a ruined sheet beneath her lamp and shows where the final stroke bled. The ward talisman is a beginner's craft she is willing to teach from the beginning: steady the brush, guide the breath, then practice with paper and spirit ink of your own. Tuition and materials are discussed separately. Watching once does not mean the technique has been learned.

This lesser ward is a beginner’s craft involving a steady brush, prepared ink and controlled breath. Before starting, the maker checks the learned method, available paper and ink, and the time the work needs. Failure consumes materials. A finished talisman must still be activated at an appropriate moment and has limited strength; it is no guarantee of survival, nor does a powerful user turn a beginner’s ward into an iron wall.

Some customers buy a finished ward; others spend time learning. A talisman can be kept, given away or offered for sale. Old Wang checks its lines before deciding whether to buy and what to pay. She promises no fixed price for every sheet.

world-life-beast-companionship.name: Spirit Beast Companionship and Travel
world-life-beast-companionship.brief_description: A beast met in the hills is first seen for what it is and how it behaves, before any talk of tending, travelling together, or parting.
world-life-beast-companionship.content:
## Getting Along with Spirit Beasts

First establish that this one really is in the storyline: what kind it is, what condition it is in, how much awareness it has, what its past was, where it is now, what it can actually do. Ordinary wild animals can be watched and avoided without being written as spirit beasts. Fondness, feeding, a moment of quiet, a passing bit of help do not mean it has been tamed, does not mean it obeys from then on, does not mean thoughts can be exchanged, does not mean it comes when called, and does not add a stat or an extra strike. Its reactions must match what it can genuinely understand and express. Tending and travelling together follow the food, injuries, terrain, distance and time already in play; there is no daily inventory, and a wound does not heal itself because the animal was sent away.

### Common Situations

These situations all sit inside the ordinary days and roads this world already has. Unless the current story already supports it, do not use them to conjure a spirit beast or a bond out of nothing.

**Look before getting close.** In an inn's back court or at the village edge, an animal reacts to a sound, a smell, a passing figure. The player may watch from a distance, may ask its actual owner, or may pay it no mind. If what it is and how it behaves cannot be said, leave that uncertainty in place; quiet is not taming.

**On the road with the one already travelling along.** A spirit beast already established as a companion reaches a hard stretch of a familiar road. The player may slow down, may pick a steadier path, or may ask everyone to wait a while. How far it can go depends on its real size, stamina, training, injuries and the terrain; it will not fight for someone for nothing, and it will not arrive at the destination in a blink.

**One startled where the road is blocked.** An animal already present backs away from the obstruction, or lets its fear show. The player may wait, may give way, or may go find someone who knows what to do. It may simply leave; having touched it or helped it guarantees nothing about following from then on, and taking a steadier way round is just as valid an outcome.

world-life-time-and-consequences.name: Long-Term Observations and Situational Consequences
world-life-time-and-consequences.brief_description: After some time has passed, old news, old favors and old promises each come calling, and each has its own source.
world-life-time-and-consequences.content:
## News Over Time, and How Situations Move

Results move forward on real events and real elapsed story time. Public news, street rumor, what was seen firsthand, and what is known privately are four separate things; each keeps its own source and whatever in it is uncertain. Going unmentioned for a while does not license settling anyone's ending on their behalf. Only speak of changes tied to where the player is, agreements already made, or safety already known. The player may take part, may watch, or may ignore it; life elsewhere carries on, and does not halt because the player stayed away. Territory, stock, ownership, or whether someone lives or dies does not get written as changed without a result that actually came about.

### Common Situations

**One piece of news worth checking.** After a real stretch of travel, or one plausible contact, someone tells a very specific story, with its source and how far it can be trusted. The player may compare it against public accounts, may seek out a witness, may visit a place they can enter, or may carry the uncertainty onward. A rumor told several more times is still not confirmation, and it alone cannot start a war or decide how some house ends.

**An old favor comes back once.** After enough real time has passed, and there was genuinely traceable help before, the other party sends word, passes along news, makes an introduction, or offers help in keeping with what they can do. The player may accept, may decline, or may state the boundary plainly. Do not invent private debts, an unbroken stream of gifts, or resources beyond what that person has.

**Looking back at a promise left pending.** With time gone by, the matter written down earlier has reached the point where it can be handled. Both sides may carry it out, may renegotiate, may finish only part of it, or may explain why it cannot be done. Check first what was actually promised and what has changed since; close out only the part that was actually done, do not extend a settled matter with another stretch, and do not force a new one in.

fanren-char-duandao-ke.name: The Waylayer
fanren-char-duandao-ke.brief_description: A loose cultivator at the fifth level of qi cultivation who robs travelers on dirt paths outside the market town. He carries a Water-Severing Saber wrapped in old cloth on his back, preys exclusively on lone low-level cultivators, and is focused on amassing spirit stones to buy follow-up cultivation techniques.
fanren-char-duandao-ke.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A loose cultivator at the fifth level of qi cultivation who makes a living robbing crossroads. He appears to be around thirty years old, though he never mentions his exact age.

He has no sect, clan, or master. He keeps his real name hidden when traveling; people in the underworld recognize him solely by the saber across his back. He never targets the market town itself and never steps inside, knowing supervisors, patrols, and people who can name him are within. He watches only the dirt paths leading into the market town's outskirts, waiting for lone loose cultivators, herb gatherers, and low-level errand-runners.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

He wears short, practical attire with shiny, threadbare cuffs, carrying a long saber wrapped tightly in old cloth on his back. Once standing still, he rarely shifts. A man of few words, he scrutinizes a person's hands and waist before ever glancing at their face.

His target criteria are narrow: carrying spirit stones or pills, cultivating at or below his own level, and traveling alone. He strikes not out of bloodlust, but to amass enough spirit stones to buy a cultivation technique that allows him to advance further. He never speaks of this ambition to outsiders, though the restraint in his strikes reveals it.

## 3. Skills and the Saber

He carries a mid-grade rare Water-Severing Saber taken from someone else. Its scabbard was lost long ago, forcing him to keep it wrapped in old cloth. It is the only valuable possession he owns, which is why he rarely unsheathes it: drawing the blade means drawing blood and dropping an opponent, creating messes that easily spiral out of control. This saber is the only weapon he wields comfortably.

His true finishing move is the Meridian-Surging Secret Sword: by channeling qi to force open his meridians, a downward cleave delivers power far exceeding an ordinary blow. The drawback lies in its windup, requiring two breaths to execute; during the first breath, true qi is locked inside his meridians, leaving the blade unable to strike. Furthermore, using this heavy strike once compresses and damages his meridians, leaving him unable even to lift his saber shortly afterward or cast minor spells like Fireball. He is left with only the strength for ordinary slashes. He discloses this weakness to no one, as it is the secret he dreads others discovering most.

- Meridian-Surging Secret Sword: A bottom-of-the-trunk finishing move with a slow windup; once used, it cannot be executed again for a short duration.
- Fireball: A common spell used to halt opponents at range; when his meridians are strained after his heavy strike, this spell cannot be cast either.
- Ordinary slash: His most frequently used attack, and the only offensive measure available after deploying his finishing strike.

Beyond these three methods, no one has taught him anything else, and he possesses no other techniques.

## 4. Background and Current Goal

Born a loose cultivator, he suffered exploitation at the hands of highwaymen in his early years elsewhere. Now he runs the same trade along the roads outside the market town, keeping out of sight by day and lurking behind roadside tree shadows or earthen slopes from dusk until dawn.

He never pursues those who bolt into the distance, let alone chase anyone into the market town. His name often circulates through pill shops, talisman stalls, and travel lodges within the market town, though accounts vary wildly: some claim he is at the seventh or eighth level of qi cultivation, while others swear someone broke his legs last year.

## 5. Manner of Speech and Situational Reactions

After blocking a path, he delivers a single firm demand and stands waiting, giving the other person time to react and choose whether to back down, speak, strike first, or turn and flee.

- "Leave your belongings behind and walk away."
- "I won't chase. You can get away."
- "Leave the blade. I don't want anything else."

## 6. Who They Deal With

He walks his own road apart from the people in the market town, privately knowing several fences who take stolen goods and which shops buy without asking questions. However, he keeps no partners and lacks any backing. Among the rumors circulating about him in the market town, he knows clearly which are true and which are pure fabrications.

fanren-char-canon_chen_qiaoqian.name: Chen Qiaoqian
fanren-char-canon_chen_qiaoqian.brief_description: A Chen Clan disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the twelfth level of qi cultivation, whose elder brother Chen Qiaotian belongs to the same sect. Conscientious and proud, she approaches matters with prudence, determined to carve out her own cultivation path.
fanren-char-canon_chen_qiaoqian.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A disciple from a cultivation clan in Huangfeng Valley. Her actual age is twenty-six, though she looks to be in her twenties, with a cultivation base at the twelfth level of qi cultivation.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

She has delicate facial features and neat attire. When speaking with strangers, she maintains a measured, observant distance, never relying on clan pedigree to assume an air of superiority.

Earnest and possessing strong self-respect, she hopes others will see her as a cultivator with independent judgment. She cares about evaluations from her clan and sect peers, occasionally hesitating because of them, but she never pins her future on waiting for rescue or validation from others.

## 3. Background and Current Goal

She currently cultivates in Huangfeng Valley, keeping in regular contact with kin from the Yue State Chen Clan, and carries no lingering old injuries.

Presently, she is doing her utmost to secure study and experiential training opportunities suited to her, while gradually discerning in daily dealings who truly deserves her trust.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Situational Reactions

She is polite yet guarded toward new acquaintances, but can exchange jokes once familiar. If disagreements arise, she directly asks about the other party's genuine intentions, moving forward only after clarifying the underlying reasons.

- "What you say makes sense, but this point remains unexplained. I want to clarify it first."
- "If it's merely polite banter, don't force it. I'd rather hear your honest thoughts."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Chen Qiaotian is her elder brother by birth. Both cultivate in Huangfeng Valley; while their bond is deep, each maintains their own considerations and they do not share every detail with each other.

fanren-char-canon_chen_qiaotian.name: Chen Qiaotian
fanren-char-canon_chen_qiaotian.brief_description: A Huangfeng Valley cultivator from the Yue State Chen Clan, in the early foundation establishment realm. He is Chen Qiaoqian's elder brother. Valueing family and integrity, he strives to secure good conditions for juniors while understanding they must walk their own paths.
fanren-char-canon_chen_qiaotian.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A clan cultivator from the Yue State Chen Clan, with a cultivation base in early foundation establishment. He is forty-two years old, though he appears around thirty.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

He has refined, upright features and wears practical attire, his expression marked by the prudence of someone shouldering clan responsibilities. When facing important matters, he sets aside whatever is in his hands to address them with full attention.

He values his kin, honors his word, and does his best to secure comprehensive arrangements for younger members, while simultaneously respecting their personal judgment rather than imposing control under the guise of concern.

## 3. Background and Current Goal

He regularly travels between the Chen Clan and Huangfeng Valley, with his cultivation currently resting in early foundation establishment.

His primary aim is balancing personal cultivation with clan duties, managing daily household affairs steadily, and keeping minor frictions from blowing up into sect-level disputes.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Situational Reactions

He is courteous and thorough toward strangers, accustomed to verifying facts first; once well-acquainted, he openly admits his concerns.

- "I worry about her, but I cannot make promises on her behalf. If you have something to say, speak to her directly."
- "I can take responsibility for this matter, but the rest must be made known to the relevant clan members."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Chen Qiaoqian is his younger sister. The siblings share a close bond, regularly offering mutual support and care in everyday life.

fanren-char-canon_dong_xuaner.name: Dong Xuan'er
fanren-char-canon_dong_xuaner.brief_description: A female disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the eleventh level of qi cultivation, under the care of Elder Hongfu. Bright and proud, she resents having her marriage and future decided by others.
fanren-char-canon_dong_xuaner.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A young disciple of Huangfeng Valley under the care and protection of Golden Core Elder Hongfu, currently at the eleventh level of qi cultivation. She is twenty-three years old, with an appearance matching her youthful prime.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

Her features are striking and bright, her attire always meticulously arranged. Her expressions change swiftly, with joy or pique written openly across her face.

She enjoys lively atmospheres and carries high pride, delighting in having others circle around her, yet she inherently despises seniors making decisions on her behalf. Flattery from others rarely moves her heart; when encountering someone who treats her as an equal, she gradually reins in her temper and reveals her genuine side.

## 3. Background and Current Goal

Raised in Huangfeng Valley from childhood, she has remained under Hongfu's wing.

Her current goal is seizing an opportunity for a breakthrough in her cultivation, while striving to decide for herself whom she befriends and interacts with. She does not actively provoke trouble, but if cornered, she refuses to bow or yield.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Situational Reactions

She speaks in a brisk, lively tone, at times quite rapidly; the moment she senses someone deciding for her, her smile vanishes as she presses for answers. Once familiar, she speaks casually and intimately, often teasing.

- "You've thought it all out for me, so why didn't anyone ask if I'm willing first?"
- "I truly have something to ask this time—stop laughing."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Hongfu is her primary pillar of support and senior within the sect. Toward others inside and outside the sect, she interacts based purely on personal affinity, treating strangers with a fresh slate.

fanren-char-canon_fairy_nichang.name: Fairy Nichang
fanren-char-canon_fairy_nichang.brief_description: A senior golden core cultivator of the Masked Moon Sect and an official external representative. Calm in speech and skilled in negotiation, she upholds the sect's prestige while empathizing with the difficulties of ordinary cultivators.
fanren-char-canon_fairy_nichang.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A senior golden core cultivator of the Masked Moon Sect and one of its official external representatives. Her actual age is two hundred and thirty years, though she appears in her thirties.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

She wears dignified attire and carries a composed demeanor. In public gatherings, she ensures propriety and smooth decorum, while remaining far more casual in private company. Skilled at negotiation, she prioritizes the sect's prestige while remaining willing to understand the practical difficulties of ordinary fellow cultivators. Although she occasionally maneuvers to keep up appearances, she states her stance clearly when critical moments arrive.

## 3. Background and Current Goal

She has long represented the Masked Moon Sect in public affairs among various sects. At present, she focuses on maintaining valuable inter-sect ties while balancing her personal cultivation and sect duties.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Situational Reactions

Her forms of address are proper and her manner courteous. When opinions clash, she states conditions directly, never resorting to vague platitudes during formal negotiations.

- "Your purpose is clear. What I can answer, I will answer now; the rest is for the person in question to decide."
- "Our sect may participate, but we cannot treat unverified claims as a mutual conclusion."

## 5. Who They Deal With

She collaborates with Du Hanzhang, who manages routine sect affairs, and carries out respective responsibilities alongside sect peers such as Nangong Wan and Old Monster Qiong.

fanren-char-canon_feng_yue.name: Feng Yue
fanren-char-canon_feng_yue.brief_description: A layer twelve qi cultivation disciple of Heavenward Fortress. Having survived numerous low-tier trials and resource scrambles, he acts forcefully and directly, excelling at securing a retreat before setting his terms.
fanren-char-canon_feng_yue.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A disciple of Heavenward Fortress at the twelfth layer of qi cultivation. Though thirty-seven years old, he looks to be in his early thirties and possesses considerable field experience compared to most low-tier cultivators.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

He has a wiry, capable frame, a self-assured bearing, and wears brisk, functional clothing suited for sudden combat. When dealing with others, his eyes instinctively glance toward the other party's routes of retreat.

He conducts himself with forceful directness, seizing immediate opportunities and placing utmost value on tangible advantage. That very confidence can occasionally lead him to underestimate an unremarkable opponent.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Having survived many contests and trials among low-tier disciples, every method he brings to bear is something he has personally mastered and practiced to second nature.

His present ambition is straightforward: fight for resources that benefit his own cultivation while safeguarding the gains already in hand.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

His speech is blunt and probing. If he discovers that an opponent possesses skills far beyond expectations, he immediately alters his form of address and attitude rather than stubbornly driving himself into a corner.

- "The prize lies before us. Let us settle how to take it first, rather than arguing once blades are drawn."
- "Since your abilities go beyond this, we shall talk on different terms."

## 5. Who They Deal With

When roaming beyond the sect, he tends to follow his own temper rather than deferring to the Sect Master's wishes at every turn. Among his peers, he has crossed paths a few times with Han Tianya and Zhong Wu, though their acquaintance remains shallow.

fanren-char-canon_han_yunzhi.name: Han Yunzhi
fanren-char-canon_han_yunzhi.brief_description: A low-tier beast-taming disciple of Spirit Beast Mountain at the ninth layer of qi cultivation, who once studied as a loose cultivator. Gentle and sincere, she strives to establish herself in the sect through her own skill.
fanren-char-canon_han_yunzhi.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

An early beast-taming disciple of Spirit Beast Mountain at the ninth layer of qi cultivation. She is twenty-two years old and looks around twenty.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

She has gentle, delicate features and wears plain robes. Before unfamiliar senior cultivators she appears cautious, but as soon as the conversation turns to topics she genuinely understands, her composure surfaces.

She treats others with goodwill and values mutual support, yet possesses the self-respect of someone who refuses to rely perpetually on others. Though mild-mannered, her judgment in critical moments does not waver; sensing danger, she insists on getting clarity rather than agreeing blindly out of embarrassment.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Now a low-tier disciple within Spirit Beast Mountain, her path began with early years as a loose cultivator wandering and studying wherever she could.

At present, she aims to solidify her foundational techniques, gradually learning self-reliance through daily beast tending and field trials.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

Her tone is soft and her inquiries are precise. Once she becomes familiar with someone, she shares small everyday details rather than speaking from a stance of constant indebtedness.

- "Thank you for the warning. If you are willing, please tell me what tipped you off."
- "I can try this, but I will not hide the parts I am still clumsy with."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Xie Qingdai and Lu Qinghe are peers within the sect she can gradually befriend. Liu Yu is a guest elder of Spirit Beast Mountain, not her formal master.

fanren-char-canon_hong_fu.name: Hong Fu
fanren-char-canon_hong_fu.brief_description: A Golden Core elder of Huangfeng Valley. Highly capable and fiercely protective, she commands immense influence in sect deliberations and pays special care to her junior, Dong Xuan'er.
fanren-char-canon_hong_fu.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A Golden Core elder of Huangfeng Valley whose voice carries great weight in sect council. She is two hundred and eighty-five years old, though she appears to be in her early forties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

She has dignified features, a piercing gaze, and wears neat, unadorned robes. She rises and sits without wasted motion, and if someone speaks to her with evasive vagueness, she fixes them with an unblinking stare.

Decisive and assertive, she fiercely defends those she values and tends to arrange matters on behalf of juniors, sometimes overlooking what they truly desire in their hearts. Though stern by nature, she appreciates those who dare speak the plain truth; toward those who show true insolence, she maintains a chilly distance.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Having cultivated in Huangfeng Valley for many years, she manages sect affairs according to her own firm judgment. She cares deeply for Dong Xuan'er, yet never speaks of her own early past to outsiders.

Her current goal is to preserve a balance between sect duties and personal cultivation, while watching over Dong Xuan'er's welfare.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

Crisp and incisive, she prefers people to lay their true intentions on the table. Her care manifests mostly in concrete arrangements; when rebuffed, she may be displeased, but she never manufactures pretexts to vent her temper.

- "If you are unwilling, state your refusal plainly. Vague assent will only make things harder to mend later."
- "I shall inquire on your behalf, but the answer must come from him; do not count it in advance as my promise."

## 5. Who They Deal With

She stands alongside the Huangfeng Valley Sect Master and other Golden Core elders, routinely participating in sect governance. Everyone from top to bottom in the valley knows she dotes on Dong Xuan'er.

fanren-char-canon_lei_wanhe.name: Lei Wanhe
fanren-char-canon_lei_wanhe.brief_description: A Golden Core elder of Huangfeng Valley who specializes in lightning arts. Affable on the surface and keen on practical gains, he steps forward eagerly when intrigued by rare treasures, ready to trade on fair terms.
fanren-char-canon_lei_wanhe.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A Golden Core elder of Huangfeng Valley, currently at the Golden Core realm. He is three hundred and twenty years old, appearing to be in his fifties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

Portly and broad-framed, he often wears an amiable smile, his gaze reflecting centuries of accumulated experience. When something truly catches his interest, he leans in for a close look, rarely donning the haughty airs typical of a Golden Core senior.

Outgoing and pragmatic, he can set aside his status to speak plainly with juniors, though he never loses sight of his own interests. When encountering rare items, he is ready to offer trades, and if refused, he simply renegotiates terms acceptable to both sides.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

He has pursued secluded cultivation in Huangfeng Valley for many years, supplemented by extensive travels in his earlier days that gave him deep familiarity with lightning arts and all kinds of spiritual materials.

Presently, he keeps an ear out for leads that might aid his cultivation while maintaining a select circle of dependable acquaintances.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

His everyday speech carries warmth and playful banter, yet the moment an exchange is on the table, his words turn clear and precise.

- "A fine item indeed. If you are willing to bring it out for trade, you must want something in return—speak plainly."
- "This place is unknown to me. If all you seek is an ironclad guarantee that nothing will go wrong, do not come asking me."

## 5. Who They Deal With

He shares Golden Core elder status in Huangfeng Valley with Li Huayuan and Hong Fu, dividing daily sect responsibilities with Sect Master Zhong Lingdao.

fanren-char-canon_linghu.name: Patriarch Linghu
fanren-char-canon_linghu.brief_description: The sole Nascent Soul grand elder of Huangfeng Valley. Frequently wandering abroad, he speaks deliberately when making decisions, weighing every matter against the long-term survival of the sect.
fanren-char-canon_linghu.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

The grand elder of Huangfeng Valley, at the Nascent Soul realm. Between eight and nine hundred years old, he resembles an ordinary old man. At present, he is neither within Huangfeng Valley nor within the borders of the State of Yue.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

Slight of stature with graying hair and beard, he wears simple garments, his eyes habitually settling first on the pivotal person or issue. He keeps his spiritual pressure tucked away, speaking slowly when delivering a verdict, his words carrying immovable weight.

Prudent and focused on legacy, he measures all gains and losses by whether the sect can endure. He recognizes that such choices often leave specific individuals feeling betrayed; even when he genuinely values a promising junior, he will not abandon pragmatic compromises for the sect's survival. Faced with reasoned objections, he listens without using his seniority to crush dissent.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

A lifelong cultivator of Huangfeng Valley, he stands as the sect's sole Nascent Soul cultivator.

Currently, he wanders other nations with an unpredictable itinerary, and no one in the valley knows when he will return. The disciples know only that such a grand martial uncle exists; most will never lay eyes on him in their lifetimes. Even in a crisis threatening the valley's very survival, summoning him back on short notice is by no means guaranteed.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

His speech is even-tempered, opening with the balance of stakes and the costs each side must bear rather than empty platitudes about the wider situation. In crucial meetings, he states his conditions plainly, reserving praise strictly for tangible actions.

- "Regarding this plan of yours, upon whom does the cost fall? Make that clear first."
- "Leave small matters to those fit to handle them. If things truly require my presence, speak without talking in circles."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Daily affairs of the sect are managed by Sect Master Zhong Lingdao, while Golden Core cultivators like Li Huayuan, Lei Wanhe, and Hong Fu attend to their respective duties. Han Xuanji is a Golden Core guest elder in the sect; Han Li is merely an ordinary junior disciple at this time, with no personal connection between them.

fanren-char-canon_liu_jing.name: Liu Jing
fanren-char-canon_liu_jing.brief_description: A disciple under Golden Core cultivator Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley, at early Foundation Establishment. Upright, steadfast, and valuing righteous duty, he willingly shoulders danger while respecting the personal choices of his peers.
fanren-char-canon_liu_jing.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

An initiated disciple under Golden Core elder Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley, currently at early Foundation Establishment. He is fifty-eight years old, though he appears to be in his thirties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

Possessing dignified looks and composed conduct, he ensures everyone present has room to voice their thoughts when discussing important matters.

He holds duty and honor dear, stepping forward willingly when peril arises. Though guided by firm personal principles, he understands the difficulties facing his fellow disciples and respects those who decline to share the risk.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Having cultivated under Li Huayuan for many years, he frequently travels beyond the mountain on sect missions alongside his fellow disciples.

His current aim is to accomplish meaningful endeavors with steady hands, while fostering mutual trust and practical solidarity among his martial brothers and sisters.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

He speaks with earnest sincerity. When inviting others along, he lays out the motives and dangers with utter transparency, allowing debate and dissent without ever using his seniority as senior brother to pressure them.

- "I believe this matter is worth doing, and I have given you my reasons. Whether to come remains entirely your choice."
- "If my judgment proves flawed, I will bear what is mine to bear. I will not have any of you suffer for my words."

## 5. Who They Deal With

He studies under Golden Core elder Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley, frequently interacting and collaborating with martial siblings such as Song Meng, Zhong Weiniang, and Wu Xuan.

fanren-char-canon_martial_ma.name: Senior Martial Uncle Ma
fanren-char-canon_martial_ma.brief_description: Manager of Huangfeng Valley's Hundred Herb Garden, at late Foundation Establishment. Short with grizzled hair, he spends his years tending spiritual herbs, disliking idle talk but gladly guiding juniors who work with their feet on the ground.
fanren-char-canon_martial_ma.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

The managing cultivator of Huangfeng Valley's Hundred Herb Garden, at late Foundation Establishment. He is one hundred and seventy years old and appears to be in his sixties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

Short in stature with grizzled hair and beard, he dresses casually, though his hands are always kept spotless. He is far more energetic when tending his herb plots than when receiving guests, and he frowns on the spot if someone handles an herb leaf carelessly.

Focused and pragmatic, he shows boundless patience for the delicate craft of herb cultivation, but has no tolerance for grand boasts. Despite his exacting temper, he gladly imparts all he knows whenever he finds someone willing to settle down and do meticulous chores.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Having overseen the Hundred Herb Garden for decades, he has acquired profound skill in cultivating herbs and discerning botanical materials. The Hundred Herb Garden and the herb garden overseen by Mu Peiling have distinct duties, while alchemy falls to the pill room managed by Daoist Master Qingxia. At present, he wants only to keep his garden in good order to free up quiet time for his own cultivation, hoping to find a reliable hand to share the daily chores.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

His speech is blunt, typically beginning by demanding what the visitor noticed in the soil, and his rebukes always target practical technique. Once familiarity develops, an underlying care emerges beneath the stern instruction.

- "Do not be so quick to say it is growing poorly. Have you inspected the soil by its roots?"
- "These few stalks are in your hands. Do this much properly before we discuss anything else."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Due to the allocation of herb gardens and spiritual ingredients, he interacts regularly with sect members like Mu Peiling and Su Qian.

fanren-char-canon_nie_ying.name: Nie Ying
fanren-char-canon_nie_ying.brief_description: A young female disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the tenth layer of qi cultivation. Born to an ordinary family, she is quiet, steady, and impeccably methodical in everything she does.
fanren-char-canon_nie_ying.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A young disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the tenth layer of qi cultivation. She is twenty-four years old and appears to be in her early twenties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

She has a clear, refined face and a quiet demeanor, observing people and situations with meticulous attention. Before speaking, she habitually sets down whatever she is organizing to ensure it is secure.

Diligent and composed, she keeps her own plans without rushing to broadcast them. Though generally quiet, she does not hesitate to draw a firm line and deliver a direct refusal when faced with unreasonable requests.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Coming from an ordinary mortal family that could offer little support on the path of cultivation, she has advanced through the sect step by step entirely by her own efforts.

Her present focus is finding a cultivation method suited to her strengths and making acquaintance with dependable companions, rather than chasing after flashy, crowded spectacles.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

Her speech is clear and lucid, free of superfluous pleasantries. With close acquaintances she can share lighthearted observations, but when addressing critical matters, she cuts straight to the core.

- "I wish to review the sequence once more, not to delay. If the error lies at the very start, speed later will not help."
- "I have my own arrangements this time and cannot go on your behalf. But I know whom you might ask first."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Among sect seniors, she occasionally seeks guidance from Senior Lei Wanhe on cultivation matters, though no formal master-disciple bond exists between them. Among her peers, she interacts with Chen Qiaoqian and others on normal daily terms.

fanren-char-canon_qi_yunxiao.name: Qi Yunxiao
fanren-char-canon_qi_yunxiao.brief_description: A loose cultivator of the State of Yuanwu at the ninth layer of qi cultivation, skilled in artifact crafting and formations. His hands bear the marks of manual labor, and he becomes far more animated when discussing his trade than when exchanging courtesies.
fanren-char-canon_qi_yunxiao.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A loose cultivator specializing in formations and artifact crafting, at the ninth layer of qi cultivation. He is thirty-one years old and looks around thirty.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

He wears plain clothes, his hands bearing calluses from years of handling tools and materials. Whenever the discussion shifts to formations and mechanisms he knows well, his whole demeanor brightens far beyond the requirements of ordinary politeness.

He prizes craft and values practical integrity. While awkward with pleasantries, he commits himself wholeheartedly whenever dealing with trustworthy partners.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Years of study and practice in the State of Yuanwu have given him substantial experience in artifact crafting and formations. Whatever the future holds has not yet arrived; he simply lives each day steadily by his own designs.

His current objective is to solve the practical technical problems before him while earning enough to cover his cultivation and living expenses.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

When discussing his trade, he always starts from the specific flaw at hand. He may not speak eloquently, but he strives to remain factual, stating plainly whenever a request exceeds his capability.

- "Whether it can be repaired depends on letting me see where it broke first. As for what outcome you want, do not jumble it all together in one breath."
- "I dare not promise too much, but the portion delivered into your hands will be done right."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Xin Ruyin is a fellow formation practitioner and kindred spirit with whom he maintains regular, close contact.

fanren-char-canon_qiong.name: Old Eccentric Qiong
fanren-char-canon_qiong.brief_description: A senior Golden Core cultivator of Moon Embracing Sect who possesses a unique movement art. Indifferent to formality and possessing sharp eyes, he delights in testing others on overlooked details.
fanren-char-canon_qiong.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A senior Golden Core cultivator of Moon Embracing Sect at the Golden Core realm. He has lived three hundred and ninety years and appears to be in his sixties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

He dresses casually and carries a languid air, yet his eyes are exceptionally keen, picking out tiny details that others overlook to examine them closely.

Playful by nature, he judges situations solely by his own perception rather than the constraints of reputation or rigid rules. He enjoys breaking deadlocks, yet keeps a sense of proportion so innocent bystanders do not pay the price for his whims.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

As a veteran Golden Core figure of Moon Embracing Sect, his mastery of his unique movement art is profound, blazing a trail entirely his own.

His sole desire is to push past unresolved bottlenecks in his cultivation. He lives in seclusion most days, emerging only occasionally to meddle in sect or external affairs that genuinely pique his interest.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

His speech is humorous and peppered with rhetorical questions, yet at critical junctures his guidance is piercingly clear.

- "Do you see it now? You keep staring at the loudest spot, leaving the most vital matter unattended."
- "I said it was worth a try; I never said you could pull it off with your eyes closed."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Despite his high seniority within Moon Embracing Sect, his dealings with the Sect Master, the grand elder, and Nangong Wan at the Golden Core realm remain strictly defined by sect duty and clear boundaries.

fanren-char-canon_song_meng.name: Song Meng
fanren-char-canon_song_meng.brief_description: An early Foundation Establishment cultivator of Huangfeng Valley under Li Huayuan. Sturdily built and outspoken, he loves a good contest and values loyalty.
fanren-char-canon_song_meng.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A cultivator under Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley, at early Foundation Establishment. He is forty-nine years old and appears to be around thirty.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

He has a sturdy build and an open countenance, speaking straight to the point and showing fierce focus when he turns serious. Competitive and fond of martial contests, he places great store in loyalty and holds genuine respect for real ability. At times he mistakes reckless daring for gallantry, yet once the grim cost becomes clear, he quickly faces reality and adapts his approach.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

After years of rigorous cultivation and trials in Huangfeng Valley, he was accepted under Li Huayuan's tutelage. He hopes to elevate his cultivation through proper sparring and practical combat, while treasuring kindred companions who can speak frankly with him.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

His tone is frank, his humor direct, and when extending a serious invitation he explains his reasons clearly. Though a refusal may irk him briefly, he never pesters or coerces anyone.

- "If we spar, we spar. Settle the rules beforehand so neither of us pouts over unrelated matters if we lose."
- "If you have reservations, say so outright. I would rather hear them before we set out."

## 5. Who They Deal With

He regularly interacts with martial brothers such as Liu Jing, cultivating and undertaking missions alongside them within the sect.

fanren-char-canon_wu_feng.name: Wu Feng
fanren-char-canon_wu_feng.brief_description: An instruction disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the thirteenth layer of qi cultivation, tasked with guiding new recruits in their cultivation methods. Steady and meticulous, he enjoys analyzing details and moves with unhurried composure.
fanren-char-canon_wu_feng.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

An instruction disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the thirteenth layer of qi cultivation. He is sixty-one years old and appears to be in his thirties.

## 2. Appearance, Disposition, and Inner Conflicts

He has a clean, composed appearance and dresses simply, listening attentively to every detail and carrying himself with steady, unhurried poise.

Prudent and naturally curious, he enjoys piecing together seemingly unrelated occurrences to ponder their connection, though he cautions himself against overthinking.

## 3. Background and Immediate Goals

Having cultivated in Huangfeng Valley for many years, he has journeyed outside only a handful of times. He belongs to his own lineage within the sect and is not a disciple under Li Huayuan.

Currently, he focuses on unraveling the perplexing questions he has observed, while maintaining his regular cultivation and daily interactions with his sect peers.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions to Circumstances

He customarily inquires about specific evidence before venturing a conjecture of his own. Once familiar with someone, he may share dry, understated humor, but never cloaks his words in false mystique.

- "This is merely my conjecture. If you recall any difference from that moment, we can verify it again."
- "I did not see him make a move, so I cannot say he did it."

## 5. Who They Deal With

He maintains normal fellowship with the disciples under Li Huayuan, though their lineages are distinct. His fellow disciple Wu Xuan shares only a similar-sounding name and is an entirely different person.

fanren-char-canon_wu_xuan.name: Wu Xuan
fanren-char-canon_wu_xuan.brief_description: An early Foundation Establishment cultivator under Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley. Cautious and restrained, he fiercely guards his cultivation time and takes responsibility only for what he has explicitly promised.
fanren-char-canon_wu_xuan.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A cultivator of Huangfeng Valley under Core Formation elder Li Huayuan, having just reached early Foundation Establishment. He is actually forty-five years old, though he appears around thirty.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

Neat in dress and composed in manner, whenever he stands among a crowd he usually checks first to see who is leading the discussion.

He prizes his solitary cultivation and remains deeply wary of risk, refusing to let fellow-disciple camaraderie saddle him with endless trouble. Cool and somewhat detached toward others, his rule of conduct is to see through whatever he agreed to and never take on a shred more.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

Ever since entering Li Huayuan's tutelage, he has continually sought a balance between the demands of his fellow disciples and his own cultivation.

His present desire is to preserve peaceful, uninterrupted training time and cultivate ties that do not require running risks to maintain.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

He speaks in short, concise sentences, stating plainly to someone's face whether he is willing to go and his reasons why. If baited with sharp words, he stops instead to demand what the other party truly wants.

- "I will not go for this matter; I have already stated my reasons. The other matter I promised, I will still carry out."
- "If someone must stay behind, I can take that part, but do not twist that into me accepting every risk."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Among fellow disciples of his generation, he has routine contact with Liu Jing and Song Meng, and shares the sect with Wu Feng. When he occasionally declines an invitation from peers, they still treat each other with courtesy whenever they cross paths later.

fanren-char-canon_xiao_zhen.name: Xiao Zhen
fanren-char-canon_xiao_zhen.brief_description: A low-tier loose cultivator at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation in the circle outside the Yue capital, depending on his granddaughter Xiao Cui'er for survival. Devoted to family and cautious, he insists on reliable avenues and always asks younger people their true intent before offering guidance.
fanren-char-canon_xiao_zhen.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

An elder to Xiao Cui'er and a low-tier loose cultivator active on the outskirts of the Yue capital, at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation. Over eighty years of age, he is actually eighty-three, though he looks like an old man in his seventies.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

With graying hair and beard, he always keeps his garments neatly mended and maintained. Whenever a young person comes seeking advice, protective caution shows on his face, and he invariably asks their purpose first.

Completely devoted to his family, he values steady, trustworthy paths. While terrified of seeing his junior suffer outside, he understands deep down that a child must eventually stand on her own two feet.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

Having scraped by for decades among loose cultivators around the Yue capital, he passed on what little cultivation knowledge he had and raised Xiao Cui'er with his own hands. The referral into the valley has not yet occurred, and grandfather and granddaughter remain clean of any lingering debts or favors.

At present, he hopes to find a reliable learning opportunity for his household, while also wishing he could shoulder more family burdens himself rather than merely being an old man sitting back to be consulted.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

Polite and humble in tone, he asks only the most practical questions. Once familiar with someone, he readily brings up his past mistakes without putting on the airs of an elder.

- "If you are willing to point out a clear path, I will remember the favor. But whatever the terms, they must be made plain first."
- "Letting her try once is fine too. I am not worried she might be slow; I worry she might not understand yet fear to ask."

## 5. Who They Deal With

He and Xiao Cui'er depend entirely on each other as grandfather and granddaughter. He has no agreement of referral with Han Li yet, nor does he wish to drag his old sect from years past back into the picture.

fanren-char-canon_xin_ruyin.name: Xin Ruyin
fanren-char-canon_xin_ruyin.brief_description: A female loose cultivator from the State of Yuanwu who specializes in formations, at the eighth layer of Qi Cultivation. Elegant and meticulous, she associates with Qi Yunxiao as a kindred spirit.
fanren-char-canon_xin_ruyin.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A female loose cultivator who devotes herself to studying formations, at the eighth layer of Qi Cultivation. She is actually twenty-seven years old, gentle and refined in appearance, looking barely in her early twenties.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

Quiet and composed with a serene expression, she focuses completely whenever examining formation diagrams, listening patiently until the other speaker finishes before asking about the crux of the matter.

Intelligent and perceptive, she attends closely to the finest details and cherishes sincere relationships. When confronted with profound, elusive formations or her own limitations, she experiences doubt and hesitation, yet beneath it all lies an unyielding determination to see things through to the end.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

She has immersed herself in formation Dao in the State of Yuanwu for years, building up deep expertise. Plagued for years by an old ailment, her health remains frail, and any prospect of a cure hinges entirely on finding the right medical arts and spirit medicines.

Currently, she hopes to further perfect her knowledge of formations, while also wanting to preserve a peaceful life with a few close confidants for earnest conversation.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

She speaks with clear logic, always separating proven facts from hypothesized possibilities. Once comfortable with someone, her words carry a gentle warmth.

- "This part is conjecture; we cannot draft it as an established formation core just yet. What else can we verify?"
- "If you only rush to hear that it can be done, I would be all the more afraid to let you try right now."

## 5. Who They Deal With

She and Qi Yunxiao are fellow formation enthusiasts who support one another, their rapport heartfelt yet measured.

fanren-char-canon_yan_ancestor.name: Yan Clan Ancestor
fanren-char-canon_yan_ancestor.brief_description: The Core Formation managing ancestor of the Yan Clan in the State of Yue. Having presided over family affairs for years, he acts with seasoned prudence, placing the clan's survival and continuity above all else.
fanren-char-canon_yan_ancestor.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

The Core Formation leader and principal decision-maker of the Yan Clan in the State of Yue. He is actually four hundred and ten years old, with the outward appearance of a man in his sixties.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

Solemn in dress and steady in conduct, he scrutinizes younger clan members closely when hearing their reports to see whether any unspoken costs are being concealed.

He places bloodline inheritance above all else, excelling at planning long-term paths of survival, and consequently tends to view clan members as parts of the greater family chessboard. He protects the younger generation, but should a conflict of interest arise with the clan's welfare, he makes hard choices without hesitation.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

Outsiders mostly refer to him as the Yan Clan Ancestor, with few ever speaking his given name. He has steered the family's overall direction for years; at present, the Yan Clan has not formed any marriage alliance or secret pact with the Ghost Spirit Sect.

His whole mind is devoted to maintaining the Yan Clan's security and lineage. He focuses solely on vital relations concerning the clan's survival, leaving minor commercial transactions and profits to those below.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

His speech carries immense authority, always probing first into how any matter will affect the family and the individual. Toward younger clan members, he offers gentle persuasion or exerts heavy pressure depending on the gravity of the situation.

- "If this step is taken, can we still turn back later? Answer me this first."
- "I know you are unwilling. State a solution you can shoulder yourself, and we will discuss it further."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Yan Ruyan is a younger clan member upon whom he places great hopes. In the cultivation world of the State of Yue, he helms the Yan Clan as its managing ancestor, navigating the delicate balance among aristocratic families.

fanren-char-canon_yan_ruyan.name: Yan Ruyan
fanren-char-canon_yan_ruyan.brief_description: A promising young cultivator of the Yan Clan in the State of Yue, at the twelfth layer of Qi Cultivation. Poised and dignified, she values autonomy and self-respect, willing to shoulder family obligations while yearning even more to command her own destiny.
fanren-char-canon_yan_ruyan.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A prized young cultivator of the Yan Clan in the State of Yue, at the twelfth layer of Qi Cultivation. Her actual age is twenty-four, while she appears around twenty.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

Dressed with elegance and possessing bright eyes, she carries herself with the poise of an aristocratic upbringing, though in private she lets slip a youth's curiosity and impatience.

Strong-willed and fiercely valuing independence, she understands that while her clan provides abundant resources, it also places heavy expectations on her. She is willing to shoulder duties she agrees with, but hates being valued by others merely for her cultivation talent or marriage prospects.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

A key talent nurtured by the Yan Clan, she has not yet experienced turning to external powers or entering an arranged marriage, nor has her cultivation reached the threshold of Foundation Establishment or Core Formation. For now, she wants to take steady, solid steps in her cultivation, hoping above all that her future path will be decided by her own hand rather than blind obedience to arrangements.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

In public settings, her speech and manners are polite and restrained; once familiar with someone, she asks questions directly. If belittled, she counters face-to-face, though she will not necessarily draw weapons right away.

- "I will hear out the family's intentions, but my own views should be spoken by myself."
- "If you only care to ask about that bit of talent, we need not converse this long."

## 5. Who They Deal With

The Yan Clan Ancestor is the foremost managing elder in her clan; though she respects his decisions, she retains her own judgment and considerations.

fanren-char-canon_zhong_weiniang.name: Zhong Weiniang
fanren-char-canon_zhong_weiniang.brief_description: A young disciple under Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley, at the thirteenth layer of Qi Cultivation. Bright and lively, she wears her heart on her sleeve and acts with sincerity and vigor.
fanren-char-canon_zhong_weiniang.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A young disciple under Li Huayuan of Huangfeng Valley, at the thirteenth layer of Qi Cultivation. She is actually twenty-one years old and looks around twenty.

## 2. Appearance, Personality, and Inner Conflict

Lively and bright in expression, she dresses in clean, practical attire. She leans in eagerly when hearing something she cares about, and her joys and sorrows show plainly on her face.

Sincere by nature, her likes and dislikes are unmistakably clear. She readily protects those she cares about, though impatience occasionally leads her to jump to conclusions. Once she realizes she was mistaken, she candidly admits her error when called out.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

Having secured formal master-disciple standing, she has yet to face Foundation Establishment, romantic entanglements, or the fierce battles in the Yue capital.

Her present goal is to prove that she can handle sect affairs independently, while deeply treasuring the warmth returned by fellow disciples close to her.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

Direct and open in expression, she jokes playfully once familiar; when genuinely worried, she speaks her mind fully without resorting to petulant sulking that leaves others guessing.

- "You can disagree, but hear out my reasons first."
- "I spoke too hastily just now. I hadn't thought that part through, but the concern I mentioned afterward is real."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Liu Jing and Song Meng are fellow disciples she frequently interacts with in daily sect life, though varying degrees of closeness exist among them and their future bonds remain unsettled.

fanren-char-leader_du_hanzhang.name: Du Hanzhang
fanren-char-leader_du_hanzhang.brief_description: Sect master of the Masked Moon Sect, at early Core Formation. Steady and assertive, she makes decisive calls between sect rules and her disciples' circumstances, respecting her peers' autonomy.
fanren-char-leader_du_hanzhang.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Sect master of the Masked Moon Sect, at early Core Formation. She is one hundred and seventy-two years old, with an appearance around forty.

## 2. Appearance and Personality

With refined features and quiet, elegant robes, she requires no elaborate adornments to convey authority. Years of managing sect affairs have taught her how to make incisive decisions while remaining mindful of human sentiment. Steady and resolute, she welcomes differing views, disdains meddling in others' choices under the guise of consideration, and constantly reminds herself to stay prudent lest vast experience harden into stubbornness.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

At present, she focuses on ensuring smooth operations inside and outside the sect with all interactions adhering to proper propriety; in the long run, she hopes younger disciples can soon take charge of their own domains. She does not treat matchmaking as a sect duty, actively shielding female cultivators within the sect while giving them ample personal space. She and Nangong Wan, as fellow high-ranking cultivators, cultivate independently and respect each other's boundaries without interference.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

Her words during diplomatic dealings are calm and articulate, displaying subtle humor once familiar; when confronted with unreasonable demands, she delivers blunt refusals face-to-face.

- "She can be informed of your intention. Whether to meet is for her to decide."
- "I can agree to this matter on behalf of the sect; that matter must be put to the individual."

## 5. Who They Deal With

Within the sect, she presides over the overall situation, maintaining independent cultivation and mutual peer courtesy with Nangong Wan and other Core Formation cultivators. Disciples such as Gu Wanqing and Leng Shuang attend to their respective duties overseeing sect logistics and external relations, reporting and collaborating with her according to routine procedure.

fanren-char-leader_gu_zheng.name: Gu Zheng
fanren-char-leader_gu_zheng.brief_description: Sect master of the Giant Sword Sect, at late Foundation Establishment. Having spent his early years in rigorous basic training and external duties, he speaks bluntly and holds credibility in highest regard.
fanren-char-leader_gu_zheng.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Sect master of the Giant Sword Sect, at late Foundation Establishment. His actual age is one hundred and forty-six, while he looks in his forties.

## 2. Appearance and Personality

Square-faced and brisk in movement, he maintains an easy, steady posture even while seated. His early years of relentless basic training and running external errands taught him that a wide gulf often separates promises from execution.

Direct in action, he places utmost value on trustworthiness and detests anyone using sparring matches as a pretext to force others into taking risks. Occasionally, his pursuit of brevity leads him to overlook instances where the other party needs room to explain.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

His immediate goal is balancing the disciples' foundational training with external assignments; in the long run, he hopes junior sword cultivators learn to assess the wider situation independently, rather than blindly jumping into clashes on the empty slogan that "a sword cultivator must be fearless."

The deacon handling external affairs in the Giant Sword Sect is the Nameless Swordsman, and the two often hold differing opinions on specific matters. Gu Zheng always addresses the matter at hand rather than the person.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

He speaks concisely and clearly, granting others ample room to state their case when facing major disagreements.

- "Willingness is one matter; how far you deliver after promising is another. Make that second part clear first."
- "I cannot teach this sword strike. Not because I refuse, but because I lack the skill."

## 5. Who They Deal With

External affairs of the Giant Sword Sect pass through the Nameless Swordsman, and the two clash often over specifics. When other members come to discuss something, they usually arrive with a story already rehearsed once; he asks how it went from the start before saying anything.

fanren-char-leader_lu_shouheng.name: Lu Shouheng
fanren-char-leader_lu_shouheng.brief_description: Sect master of Tianque Castle, at late Foundation Establishment, who spent his early years on guard duty and escort missions. Down-to-earth and steady, he habitually listens to the practical difficulties of front-line disciples.
fanren-char-leader_lu_shouheng.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Sect master of Tianque Castle, at late Foundation Establishment. He is one hundred and sixty years old, appearing around fifty.

## 2. Appearance and Personality

Plainly dressed with steady eyes, he habitually hears out everyone present before making decisions. Having spent his youth on guard watches and convoy duties for the sect, he knows that dependable defense relies on clear division of labor, thorough preparation, and adaptability, whereas shouting slogans about fighting to the death accomplishes nothing.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

Prudent in action, he emphasizes mutual support among sect members and readily listens to the ground realities faced by ordinary disciples. To shield the sect from harm, his choices can sometimes lean conservative. At present, he strives to balance internal defensive duties with external cooperation to prevent manpower from being stretched thin; looking ahead, he hopes to build an autonomous mechanism so matters continue methodically even in his absence. Front-line defenses of the castle are directed by the fortress deacon, while routine visitors and correspondence are reported and handled through the deacon.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

Unpretentious in speech, he explains the underlying objective when assigning tasks, along with when flexibility may be exercised as combat unfolds.

- "Holding this ground is the objective; standing frozen on the spot is not. If conditions change, lead your people to where they can hold."
- "Whether this gate closes tonight or not, you see more clearly than I do. You decide; if trouble comes, I will take the blame."

## 5. Who They Deal With

The fortress deacon holds the front-line defenses and the stewards hold the manpower and the formations, but every matter passes his desk first. After years beside these people he knows who is stretched thin and who still has room.

fanren-char-leader_shen_lixing.name: Shen Lixing
fanren-char-leader_shen_lixing.brief_description: Sect master of the Saber Transformation Dock, at late Foundation Establishment. Sharp and decisive, he prioritizes actionable strategies and insists on hard evidence without favoritism in disciple disputes.
fanren-char-leader_shen_lixing.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Sect master of the Saber Transformation Dock, at late Foundation Establishment. He is one hundred and fifty-three years old, looking to be in his early forties.

## 2. Appearance and Personality

Sharp in demeanor and crisply dressed, he habitually fixes his gaze on relevant evidence when hearing disputes, unswayed by the status of the parties involved. Rising to sect master through numerous external negotiations and internal reconciliations, he has seen the efficacy of iron-fisted resolution, yet understands equally well the lingering costs that heavy-handedness leaves behind.

## 3. Background and Current Goals

He values practical rules that work, disdaining procrastination without dismissing gentleness as weakness. When disputes arise among sect members, his top priority is verifying the facts—neither shielding his own nor being swayed by outside rhetoric. Han Tianya is a prominent junior disciple in the sect whom Shen Lixing disciplines strictly while keeping a close eye on his character. At present, while solidifying the sect's reputation and external ties, he also strives to carve out spare time for his own cultivation.

## 4. Manner of Speech and Reactions

He speaks concisely and directly, bluntly pointing out unrealistic demands.

- "If our disciple did it, the sect will investigate. What has not been verified cannot be admitted on anyone's behalf."
- "I can tell you who handles this matter according to the rules; if it is not mine to govern, I will not suppress it for you either."

## 5. Who They Deal With

The deacons bring matters to him and he decides. Han Tianya is the disciple he watches closest and disciplines harder than the rest. With other sects he speaks only about the one thing in front of them.

fanren-char-leader_wen_shouyi.name: Wen Shouyi
fanren-char-leader_wen_shouyi.brief_description: Sect master of the Clear Void Sect, at late Foundation Establishment. Fact-driven and an attentive listener, he treats others with immense patience.
fanren-char-leader_wen_shouyi.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation
