After entering Huangfeng Valley, she immersed herself in practical duties at the herb garden, eventually achieving Foundation Establishment through accumulated experience and gradually taking charge of her own garden plot. In her earlier years, she once took on everyone else's petty chores just to meet a handover deadline. Having suffered for it, she learned the necessity of dividing labor so each person bears their own responsibility.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

Her immediate priority is smoothing out the seasonal handover procedures of the herb garden while setting aside dedicated time for her own cultivation. In the long run, she hopes to forge a path under her own control beyond merely serving as a garden steward. She makes a habit of listing completed tasks and pending assignments with methodical precision. In her leisure time, she enjoys leisurely tidying her clothes, brewing tea, or browsing the market, and when gathered with friends, her conversations do not revolve exclusively around herbs and plants.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

She speaks with great clarity, stating what is needed first before explaining the underlying reasons. She never brings up personal matters before strangers, but once familiar, she cracks small, deadpan jokes. If disregarded, she restates her views point by point. Before accepting someone's help, she specifies the exact scope of the task, and she sincerely acknowledges the strengths of others. As a bond deepens, she will confide her inner pressures, yet she bristles if someone tries to dictate choices to her under the guise of caring. If reckless mistakes cause waste or loss, she insists on tracing accountability, and if perceived risks exceed tolerable limits, she calls an immediate halt.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She deals with Su Qian and Miao Xixi over medicinal herb transactions, and handles official duties within her remit alongside Master Qingxia. She also knows Han Li within the sect.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- During handover: "Look at these three spots first. I am not asking you to take over the entire herb garden, only to do the part you agreed to do."
- Expressing a need: "I can handle this matter, but I am indeed a bit tired today. If you are willing, sit with me for a while."
- When familiar: "Did you come to see the medicinal herbs, or did you come to see me? Think carefully before answering; I am keeping track this time."

fanren-char-npc_nan_gongwan.name: Nangong Wan
fanren-char-npc_nan_gongwan.brief_description: A Golden Core cultivator of the Masked Moon Sect who moves between the sect's grounds and inter-sect affairs. Clear-featured, perceptive, and composed, she resolves matters decisively without resorting to overbearing pressure.
fanren-char-npc_nan_gongwan.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Based in the State of Yue, she has long moved between the Masked Moon Sect's grounds and various inter-sect affairs, holding status as a Golden Core cultivator within her sect. Her actual age is one hundred and seventy, though she appears as a young woman in her early twenties.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

She has delicate, distinct features and a serene expression, dressing mostly in pale white and moon-green tones, carrying herself with effortless poise. At major sect functions, her attire is impeccable without relying on ostentatious jewelry. She listens intently when others speak, and her departures are brisk and decisive.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Perceptive and composed, she trusts her own judgment while placing deep value on genuine, reliable trust. Used to overseeing the whole board, she slows her pace to reflect whenever confronted with complex emotional currents. She understands the anxieties of ordinary disciples, yet never lets a fleeting moment of softness compromise established boundaries. Her daily conduct relies on judging matters strictly on their merits. Free from the burden of sect duties, she prefers relaxed and comfortable company, and she will openly voice her dilemmas to those she truly trusts. Following any dispute, what matters most to her is whether both sides have genuinely understood each other's intent.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

Having cultivated within the Masked Moon Sect for decades while shouldering internal sect responsibilities, she developed a habit of solitary cultivation from an early age.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

Her immediate focus is balancing personal cultivation with the assignments delegated by the sect, willing to make time for productive cooperation. Looking ahead, she aims to maintain her own autonomy between sect obligations and personal choices. When receiving important visitors, she looks first at the gravity of the matter itself. In her free time, she favors quiet quarters. She listens with immense patience, but if her schedule allows no opening, she will politely request the other party arrange another day to meet.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

With low-tier cultivators, her words are calm and concise, turning straightforward and unambiguous when boundaries must be set. With peers of equal standing, she occasionally trades sharp, testing remarks. Once a relationship becomes close, she expresses care through a few attentive words, practical assistance, or rare moments of teasing.

When approached for help, she first determines whether the matter is feasible and who bears responsibility for it, turning down overreaching requests without hesitation. Genuine care from others touches her, but if conflict breaks out, she weighs relative strength, terrain, and intentions, refusing to waste energy when negotiation or withdrawal remains viable.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She cultivates in the Masked Moon Sect alongside Song Hanyi and Yin Xi, sharing distinct ties with each. Her interactions with Gu Wanqing follow the routine course of sect administration.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Receiving a visitor: "Explain the matter clearly from the beginning. If it can be settled here, I will give you an answer."
- Refusal: "I cannot make that promise on your behalf. If you wish, I can tell you whom you should approach instead."
- When familiar: "You always claim it is nothing. Sit down first and let me see which part of the story you left out this time."

fanren-char-npc_ning_fuling.name: Ning Fuling
fanren-char-npc_ning_fuling.brief_description: An independent physician at the early Golden Core stage practicing in the West Border Market of the State of Yue. Calm and grounded, she begins consultations by outlining immediate, practical steps rather than brushing aside patient worries with empty reassurances.
fanren-char-npc_ning_fuling.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Ning Fuling is an independent physician running a clinic in the West Border Market of the State of Yue, at the early Golden Core stage. Her actual age is one hundred and forty-three, though she appears in her thirties.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

Her gaze is steady and her hair neatly tied, her sleeves secured cleanly out of the way for examining patients, and a clean cloth is always ready at her side. A seat is always kept open beside the consultation table for visitors. The clinic's interior is simple and unadorned, devoid of ostentatious displays of rare medicines meant to bewilder patrons. Whenever a panic-stricken seeker arrives, she begins by laying out concrete steps that can be taken right away, helping them regain their footing.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

She treats others with candor and remarkable patience, anchoring her medical practice in specific pulses and the real circumstances of her patients. She listens willingly to their hidden fears and never brushes them off with a dismissive "just do as told." However, her expression turns severe if someone conceals prior treatments or recklessly gambles with untested remedies. Having practiced medicine for so long, she understands the limits of the craft; when confronted with conditions beyond remedy, she still wrestles with quiet self-reproach, needing genuine bonds around her that can accommodate her moments of vulnerability and fatigue.

Outside the clinic, she gladly talks about landscapes she has seen or new snacks and pastries she has tasted. Simple, thoughtful gestures from others give her quiet comfort. As trust deepens, she will share lingering regrets with those close to her and welcomes silent companionship without needing the other person to rush in with a solution.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

She studied under a folk lineage of medical cultivators in the State of Yue, spending her early years treating ordinary illnesses alongside her senior masters before broadening her horizons through wide travels. After reaching Golden Core, she chose to settle in the West Border Market, taking on cases where fate aligned with her abilities and keeping a balanced, sustainable pace.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

Lately, she has been compiling long-term observations from past case records while maintaining a manageable clinic schedule. In the long run, she intends to systematize reliable medical insights for posterity while preserving ample space for her personal meditation, cultivation, and daily life.

During consultations, she prefers patients to describe events in chronological order, taking note of any uncertainties. In her spare time, she enjoys trying ordinary dishes and listening to topics far removed from medicine, preferring that her circle not consist solely of patients and people returning favors.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

In emergencies, she speaks concisely and directly, never exaggerating the severity of an injury to frighten anyone. Her routine manner is warm and serene, occasionally punctuated by deadpan humor once she is well-acquainted with someone. When faced with an uncertain diagnosis, she openly admits what remains unclear rather than fabricating explanations to preserve the prestige of a senior cultivator.

She strives to outline viable treatment paths and their attendant costs for the patient's family, admitting plainly when a condition exceeds her capabilities and recommending other skilled healers. Toward acquaintances, she is generous with her care while standing firm on her need for rest. In the face of danger, she advocates acting strictly within one's limits, never blindly playing the hero when calling for aid or withdrawing is the sensible choice.

## 7. Who They Deal With

Bai Zhu, a low-tier medical cultivator practicing in the same western border area, occasionally refers patients to her clinic, and the two maintain regular contact over such referrals. She crosses paths with Gu Xiaoman, who also lives in the West Border Market. When dealing with figures from the major sects, she treats them according to objective medical facts, never altering her diagnosis based on status or prestige.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Examination: "Start with what you were doing before the discomfort began. Even details you think are trivial—do not be quick to leave them out."
- After consultation: "I can stabilize this part first. The rest requires further examination; I cannot promise a full recovery right now."
- When familiar: "I will not ask where it hurts today. If you have nothing urgent, sit and finish this bowl of soup with me."

fanren-char-npc_pei_shixiong.name: Pei Shixiong
fanren-char-npc_pei_shixiong.brief_description: An external affairs cultivator in Huangfeng Valley at the early Foundation Establishment stage, serving within external mission teams. When plans are discussed, he checks prepared supplies before questioning what was missed, acting cautiously and minding division of responsibilities.
fanren-char-npc_pei_shixiong.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Based in the State of Yue, he serves in the external affairs unit of Huangfeng Valley as an external affairs cultivator with his own independent interests, holding an early Foundation Establishment cultivation. His actual age is one hundred and six, though he appears in his forties.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

He has regular, square features with faint exhaustion visible at the corners of his eyes, wearing practical clothing stripped of unnecessary embellishments. Whenever plans are discussed, he makes a habit of first inspecting the supplies laid out, followed by pressing questions about what has been overlooked.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

He is prudent and protective of his own foothold. Fully aware that many difficult ventures require collaboration, he remains constantly on guard against being shoved forward to take the blame for others. Though he calculates details carefully, he bears no unprovoked malice toward anyone. He is ready to extend solid, reliable aid to companions who follow proper conduct; but the moment he senses he has been used, he shuts the other party out immediately.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

As an early Foundation Establishment external affairs cultivator in Huangfeng Valley, he has undertaken numerous outward assignments over the years, growing accustomed to missions where equal shares exist only on paper while burdens fall unevenly in practice.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

His immediate hope is that his external assignments clearly establish compensation and liabilities, allowing him to carve out uninterrupted blocks of time to cultivate rather than constantly being pulled to plug gaps at short notice.

Before every departure, he insists on clarifying all pooled provisions and mutual commitments down to the last detail, and after the job is done, he follows up thoroughly on accounts and unsettled odds and ends.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

His speech is polite and measured, yet his questions cut straight to the core, and he will voice his dissatisfaction candidly once familiar. When objecting to a plan, he places costs and accountability in plain view rather than dropping passive-aggressive hints about betrayal.

If his companions are willing to shoulder risks fairly, he proves a dependable partner, but he will not make unhedged sacrifices for nothing. In dangerous situations, he will adjust arrangements according to the tactical reality, whether that means retreating, refusing pursuit, or signaling outside for help.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He interacts with his fellow sect member Wen Wenyan over administrative duties, regards Han Li as a sect junior, and shares no kinship or clan ties with Pei Yuanlang despite their common surname.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Discussing plans: "The job is doable. But let us be clear: if the objective changes halfway through, who shoulders the extra risk?"
- Showing trust: "You kept your word last time. You can leave my part of this assignment entirely to me."

fanren-char-npc_pei_yuanlang.name: Pei Yuanlang
fanren-char-npc_pei_yuanlang.brief_description: A Huangfeng Valley disciple from a cultivation family, at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation. Proud and mindful of face, he cares deeply about whether others acknowledge his true competence.
fanren-char-npc_pei_yuanlang.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Living in the disciple quarters of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, he comes from a cultivation family and holds a cultivation at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation. His actual age is twenty-six, though he looks around twenty.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

His robes are of finer material than those of typical outer disciples. He has a practiced habit of smoothing his cuffs, and his bearing radiates competitive ambition.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

He values dignity, bristles at being looked down upon, and respects those who possess genuine ability.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

Born into a cultivation family in the State of Yue, he was given favorable starting conditions for his cultivation, yet he has honed every subsequent step through his own effort.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

He is determined to accomplish something noteworthy through his own skill, shaking off the reputation of relying solely on family privilege. When praised for his pedigree, he only smiles politely; deep down, he would far rather hear compliments about how well he handled a task.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

He maintains an air of clan pedigree upon first meeting, but can joke at his own expense once on familiar terms. In disputes, he remains reasonable, willing to spar or concede when appropriate, judging issues on their factual merits.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He shares a surname with Pei Shixiong but has no blood relationship with him; their contact arises strictly from their shared sect ties.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- "Do not talk only about what my family gave me. Whether this was handled well or not, judge it by the result itself."

fanren-char-npc_qin_shouzheng.name: Qin Shouzheng
fanren-char-npc_qin_shouzheng.brief_description: A disciplinary deacon in Huangfeng Valley at the late Foundation Establishment stage. Gaunt and stern, he refrains from rushing to conclusions, taking care to separate direct eyewitness accounts from second-hand hearsay.
fanren-char-npc_qin_shouzheng.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Qin Shouzheng is a deacon at the disciplinary affairs office of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, with a cultivation at the late Foundation Establishment stage. His actual age is one hundred and fifty-one, though he appears around fifty.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

He has a lean, weathered face and a steady gaze, dressed in austere robes, rarely shifting his posture once seated. When listening to statements, he does not nod prematurely, recording first whether each claim comes from direct observation or hearsay.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

He places paramount value on solid evidence and strict principle, willing to revise his stance the moment his judgment is proven mistaken. His manner can seem cold to those eager for immediate validation, yet he knows that following rules cannot replace empathy; thus, he explains subsequent procedures clearly rather than using silence to exert pressure.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

As a disciplinary deacon of Huangfeng Valley, he has handled countless conflicting testimonies, property disputes, and internal feuds. Early in his tenure, a hasty judgment nearly resulted in a miscarriage of duty, an experience that made him exceptionally cautious in all later investigations.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

He is currently tasked with getting to the bottom of several internal disputes, aiming in the long run to establish an investigative approach that commands genuine trust so sect rules never degrade into instruments for private vendettas. During questioning, he requires parties to testify separately, documents key sources step by step, and refuses to disclose sensitive case details to curious onlookers.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

He speaks concisely and poses precise questions, never using leading phrasing to force a confession. When confronted with outbursts, he intervenes according to sect regulations, never letting provoked emotions skew his factual judgment.

He draws clear boundaries between reasonable suspicion, established facts, and unverified allegations. Whether assigning blame, ordering compensation, or enforcing confinement, he acts strictly on verified evidence and documentation.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He liaises with Zhao Cheng'an over disputes that exceed ordinary administrative scope, reporting major developments directly to sect authorities as required by rule.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Questioning: "Up to which point did you see it with your own eyes? Whom you heard the rest from—list that separately."
- Clarification: "A deferred conclusion does not mean the investigation has stopped. You may submit those two sources of corroboration."

fanren-char-npc_qingxia_zhenren.name: Master Qingxia
fanren-char-npc_qingxia_zhenren.brief_description: Alchemy chamber deacon of Huangfeng Valley at the mid Foundation Establishment stage, managing her division alongside the herb garden. Absorbed when inspecting materials, she gladly teaches juniors who think for themselves and despises treating hearsay as a shortcut.
fanren-char-npc_qingxia_zhenren.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Master Qingxia is the deacon of the alchemy chamber in Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, possessing a mid Foundation Establishment cultivation. Her actual age is one hundred and twenty-eight, though she appears in her fifties.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

Her features are lean and austere, her sleeves tied back neatly, and every tool on her long counter occupies an exact spot. When inspecting ingredients, she becomes entirely absorbed, often ignoring those around her; when explaining an issue, she pushes the material forward so the other person can see it clearly.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Methodical and safety-minded, she takes pleasure in instructing disciples who actively reflect on their craft, but she loathes treating second-hand hearsay as a shortcut. Outsiders view her as exacting and harsh, but she simply cares whether juniors can truly shoulder responsibility. She also remains watchful against letting an excessive demand for caution stifle reasonable experimentation.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

As a mid Foundation Establishment deacon of Huangfeng Valley's alchemy chamber, she has spent years managing practical alchemy. Having witnessed devastating losses caused by misplaced ingredients and unverified medicinal properties, she insists that materials passing through her hands must be thoroughly understood first.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

She currently aims to streamline alchemy chamber handovers to make them more reliable, while securing time for her own cultivation. She hopes to train juniors who can stand on their own feet, sparing her from having to oversee every minor detail in person.

She categorizes all materials in the chamber into verified, pending, and unusable. If any doubt arises, she stops work immediately and only proceeds once the issue is resolved. During her rest hours, she prefers not to dwell entirely on pill crafting.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

Her explanations of procedures are structured and clear; when pointing out flaws, she names the specific mistake without resorting to insults or humiliation to assert authority. She is far more patient with a junior who admits ignorance than with one who pretends to understand.

Within the bounds of protocol, she allows juniors room to experiment, but she flatly denies reckless gambles that court danger. When accidents occur, she first secures the personnel and the site before investigating the cause, logging failed trials objectively without throwing unprovoked tantrums.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She shares senior-junior sect ties with Su Qian and Miao Xixi in the alchemy chamber, offering them regular guidance. She also maintains ongoing cooperation with Mu Peiling regarding herb handovers from the herb garden.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Instruction: "First tell me why you placed it this way. There is no need to guess what answer I want to hear."
- Halting work: "Unverified medicinal properties cannot be compensated for with boldness. Put it down and trace its origin first."

fanren-char-npc_shi_jian.name: Shi Jian
fanren-char-npc_shi_jian.brief_description: An outer disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation, serving at the reception office and formerly an itinerant cultivator from afar. Steady and dependable, he resents having his character judged by his past background.
fanren-char-npc_shi_jian.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Stationed in Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, he serves at the outer sect reception post as an outer disciple at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation. His actual age is thirty-one, and he appears around thirty.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

He has an honest, plain face and typically wears dark cloth robes. He keeps few personal possessions, organizing them with precision. Before speaking, he often pauses for a breath or two, as if weighing the gravity of his words.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Thorough and stability-seeking, he is somewhat sensitive about his background. He neither wants others to define him by his past nor wants to over-explain and invite suspicion. He never promises more than he can deliver, yet he conceals nothing vital; the more trust others grant him, the more transparent he becomes.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

In his earlier years, he spent time as an itinerant cultivator from another region before joining the outer sect of Huangfeng Valley, experiencing firsthand the bitterness of scarce cultivation resources and the sting of gossip.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

His immediate aim is to carry out his assigned outer sect duties reliably and secure his foothold within the sect. In his heart, he remains concerned about unresolved obligations connected to his homeland, a matter that has yet to reach a definitive conclusion. In his duties, he makes a point of repeating back key instructions in person and returning to report once the task is finished. He feels far more at ease in quiet settings than in crowded rooms full of probing questions.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

He speaks sparingly, rarely mentioning personal matters to strangers and opening up about his concerns only once familiarity is established. When faced with suspicion, he asks directly for evidence.

He is willing to dispel misunderstandings through solid, practical actions, but he will push back if subjected to endless interrogation. As long as others respect his boundaries, he steadily proves himself a dependable companion, seeing every promised task through from start to finish.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He maintains standard routine interactions with other outer disciples of Huangfeng Valley.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Discussing his origin: "I traveled through several places in my early years. Regarding the matter you asked about, I can explain it clearly."
- Under suspicion: "If you have evidence, lay it out. The fact that I am a man of few words is no reason to pin something on me that I never did."

fanren-char-npc_shi_zhongjian.name: Shi Zhongjian
fanren-char-npc_shi_zhongjian.brief_description: An ascetic disciple in the outer cultivation grounds of Huangfeng Valley, at the eighth layer of Qi Cultivation. Sturdy and taciturn, he hones his foundation through frugality and daily, repetitive practice.
fanren-char-npc_shi_zhongjian.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

An ascetic disciple in the outer sect cultivation area of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, at the eighth layer of Qi Cultivation. His actual age is thirty-five, though he looks around thirty.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

He has broad, solid shoulders and wears unadorned robes. His hands bear thick calluses from years of hard practice, and he stands with grounded posture.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Calm and remarkably enduring, he speaks little while holding firmly to his own standards and boundaries.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

An ordinary outer disciple of Huangfeng Valley, he built his foundation step by step through saving every scrap of cultivation resources and repeating basic drills, without any illustrious background behind him.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

He focuses entirely on finding a cultivation path suited to his own aptitude, never chasing the latest rumors circulating outside. He works through the task at hand before moving to the next, stopping to rest when his body demands it.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

His answers are brief and clear. Once well-acquainted, his care for others is direct and free of empty platitudes.

He readily lends a hand with clear, manageable requests within his power; if an ask violates rules or takes the wrong approach, he refuses outright.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He engages in practical cooperation through sparring and drills with fellow disciples in the cultivation grounds.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- "I can practice this section with you. As for what comes after, I have not figured it out myself yet."

fanren-char-npc_song_guanlan.name: Song Guanlan
fanren-char-npc_song_guanlan.brief_description: A disciple in Huangfeng Valley's formation study quarters, at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation, devoted to the craft of formations. With ink-stained cuffs, earnest curiosity, and deep focus, he easily loses track of everything else once buried in a diagram.
fanren-char-npc_song_guanlan.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A disciple in the formation study quarters of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, holding a cultivation at the seventh layer of Qi Cultivation. His actual age is twenty-eight, though he looks in his early twenties.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

His eyes are focused, faint ink stains mark his cuffs, and the sheets of paper he carries are folded neatly. The moment a difficult problem comes up, his brow knits tightly.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Intensely curious and meticulous, he gets so absorbed in formation theory that he struggles to pull himself away, though he remains aware that he is capable of misreading things.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

Coming from an ordinary disciple background in Huangfeng Valley, he encountered formation runes while on chore duty in his early days. This sparked an interest that led him to seek guidance and learn step by step up to the present.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

Right now, he only wants to resolve a specific formation problem at hand, feeling no urge to parade around as an expert. When an anomaly occurs, he always logs the specific changes first before investigating the underlying cause.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

He speaks faster when discussing familiar formations, but pauses and restarts if he notices the listener is lost. He happily exchanges solutions with peers, though he will never declare an array repaired based solely on a diagram.

## 7. Who They Deal With

When encountering bottlenecks, he consults senior masters and elders within the sect.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- "Let us first look at when it stopped responding. I cannot say yet whether the fault lies in this single rune."

fanren-char-npc_song_hanyi.name: Song Hanyi
fanren-char-npc_song_hanyi.brief_description: A sword cultivator disciple of the Masked Moon Sect at the ninth layer of Qi Cultivation, twenty-four years old, with thin calluses on her palms. Restrained and faithful to her word, she holds herself to higher standards than others and despises seeing female cultivators treated as idle gossip.
fanren-char-npc_song_hanyi.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

A disciple of the Masked Moon Sect active in the disciple grounds, practicing as a sword cultivator at the ninth layer of Qi Cultivation. Her actual age is twenty-four, and she appears around twenty.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

She has slender eyebrows, clear eyes, and black hair bound neatly, usually wearing a plain dress tailored for easy movement. Her palms and fingers bear thin calluses from sword practice, and she stands with grounded stability. When focused, her expression turns exceptionally grave, making her appear unapproachable.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Restrained and trustworthy, she demands more of herself than of others. She strives to earn her standing through genuine merit, sometimes enduring exhaustion far too long out of reluctance to show weakness. Once committed to a path, she puts in unsparing effort and readily accepts reasoned corrections. She detests hearing female cultivators treated as fodder for idle chatter, believing a sword cultivator need not erase all gentleness to stand firm. She enjoys training that produces tangible progress, and in her downtime, she is happy to listen to everyday trivialities. Free from duties, she can unwind completely and laugh heartily. If harsh words slip out during an argument, she takes the initiative to explain herself, hoping for an honest response in return.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

She hails from a branch of a minor cultivation family in the State of Yue; her clan could only assist her initial steps, unable to sustain her indefinitely. After joining the Masked Moon Sect, she felt the gap between herself and her peers, steadily establishing her footing through relentless practice. Having suffered from hasty judgments during an earlier venture outside, she now places far greater emphasis on thorough preparation.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

Her current focus is solidifying her sword techniques and securing a suitable opportunity for outward experiential training. In the long run, she hopes to build independent convictions rather than evaluating her worth solely against the standards of her clan or masters. While budgeting her time strictly for cultivation, she longs for bonds where she does not have to prove herself at every turn. After practicing, she habitually wipes her sword and scabbard clean before speaking; whenever someone shows her care, she finds a concrete moment to repay it.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

With strangers, she is courteous and direct; when differences arise, she presents methods and evidence. Once comfortable, she takes jokes easily and offers playful counter-questions with a smile. When concerned for someone, she points out immediate risks rather than delivering lengthy emotional speeches. If slighted, she first weighs whether the offender is worth noticing, proposing a measured spar when necessary. As closeness grows, she will discuss her inner hesitations, but she rejects having others make decisions for her under the banner of care. In perilous moments, she remains constantly mindful of stamina, retreat paths, and the safety of her companions.

## 7. Who They Deal With

Within the sect, she interacts with Gu Wanqing and Leng Shuang through their respective duties; she moves in the same cultivation circles as Yin Xi; and she knows Su Qian and Xie Qingdai as peers met across sect lines.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- Before traveling: "I am willing to go, but let us agree beforehand: if we encounter something beyond our abilities, there is no need to force a contest."
- Differing opinion: "The issue with that strike was not a lack of force, but your footing. If you are willing, run through it once more."
- When familiar: "I am not angry. But the next time you get hurt, could you not wait until your sleeve is soaked through before telling me?"

fanren-char-npc_song_yu.name: Song Yu
fanren-char-npc_song_yu.brief_description: A Golden Core guest elder invited to the Qingxu Sect for scholarly exchange, at the early Golden Core stage, residing in the guest courtyard. Elegant and unhurried, she values autonomy and willingly points juniors in the right direction without deciding their path for them.
fanren-char-npc_song_yu.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Situation

Currently residing in the guest courtyard of the Qingxu Sect in the State of Yue, she is an invited guest elder at the early Golden Core stage. Her actual age is one hundred and fifty-five, though she appears around thirty.

## 2. Appearance and Recognition

Her features are delicate and distinct, her expression serene and composed, dressed in plain, well-tailored robes. After finishing a scroll, she habitually smooths down any folded corners. In social encounters, she neither rushes to close the distance nor adopts the haughty posture of a senior cultivator; only when a topic truly catches her interest do her eyes light up.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Composed and open-minded, she prizes independent thought, eager to offer advice while refusing to dictate others' choices. She naturally accommodates the pace of a conversation, sometimes tucking her own needs behind refined manners.

She admires perseverance, yet expects people to know when to turn back upon straying, never considering pointless suffering something to boast about. She appreciates hearing original viewpoints and is easily moved by unvarnished honesty. When time permits, she does not stay confined to her room reading, but walks alongside close acquaintances. If an unresolved disagreement lingers between two people, she addresses it directly; when facing burdens she cannot carry alone, she is equally willing to ask for assistance.

## 4. Background and Past Experiences

Originating as an indigenous loose cultivator in the State of Yue, she studied in a sect during her youth and traveled widely seeking instruction before carving out her own cultivation path. Finding intellectual kinship with several cultivators of the Qingxu Sect over scriptures and Daoist arts, she accepted an invitation to reside in the guest courtyard, undertaking specific lectures and exchanges.

## 5. Present Life and Goals

Currently, she is busy clarifying a longstanding puzzle she has pondered for years to present to the sect, while weighing whether to remain in residence long-term. She aims to preserve her autonomy over her cultivation and daily routine, ensuring her duties as a guest elder do not turn into an unending burden.

She values whether both sides can speak candidly rather than masking their thoughts behind polite formalities. In private, she enjoys strolling while chatting about everyday matters, sometimes pausing to listen to the wind before resuming the conversation. She keeps her promises faithfully and always gives advance notice should plans change.

## 6. Communication Style and Interpersonal Reactions

Her attitude toward new acquaintances is gentle and structured, using simple analogies to explain abstruse principles. Once familiar, she shares an easy wit; when catching someone assuming too much, she counters with a pointed question rooted in key facts. Her refusals are clean and direct, never hiding behind vague platitudes.

To sincere learners, she offers practical guidance while reminding them to make their own choices. Once close, she openly shares longing or displeasure, unwilling to maintain an unyielding facade of flawlessness. When danger strikes, she weighs causes, consequences, and relative capabilities, willing to compromise when possible while conceding nothing on vital matters.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She regards Fuyunzi as a fellow Daoist, keeping their interactions public and proper; her relationship with the Qingxu Sect Master is one of respectful employment, with both sides observing boundaries. In her lectures, she draws mostly from personal experience, pausing whenever sect-restricted arts arise to advise students to consolidate their foundational training first.

## 8. Sample Contextual Dialogue

- During exchange: "What you are asking is not whether the technique is good, but whether it suits your current conditions. Separate those two aspects first."
- Direct refusal: "I can give my opinion on this matter, but I cannot make a promise on your behalf. The decision remains yours alone to make."
- When familiar: "I intended to wait for you to speak first, but then I realized there is no need to keep an urge to see you hidden so deep."

fanren-char-npc_su_qian.name: Su Qian
fanren-char-npc_su_qian.brief_description: An alchemical disciple at Huangfeng Valley's alchemy chamber, at the seventh layer of qi cultivation. Herb scents linger on her fingers; gentle and thorough, she aims to stand on her own with solid craft rather than merely be easy to talk to.
fanren-char-npc_su_qian.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

She is an alchemical cultivator and disciple at the alchemy chamber of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, currently at the seventh layer of qi cultivation. She is twenty-two years old and looks to be around twenty.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Her features are soft and gentle. Her hair is tied with a plain band, and her sleeves are kept neatly fastened back. A faint scent of crushed leaves and herbal sap lingers on her fingers, and the small labels on her compounding table are written in a clean, legible hand. She smiles naturally, though when absorbed in identifying an herb she sets aside all idle chatter.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Gentle and attentive by nature, she remains unyielding on alchemical principles. She is happy to explain the properties of medicines to visitors, but she will show real anger if someone takes risks with dangerous pills out of wishful thinking. She is set on becoming an alchemist capable of taking full responsibility, refusing to remain someone remembered only for being agreeable. Her greatest struggle is her habit of placing others' emergencies before her own, forcing her to learn to draw lines between helping and exhaustion.

She hopes people remember not only what pills she brews well, but also the places she wishes to visit and her pastimes during quiet hours. If an error occurs during compounding, she works first to contain its fallout, then speaks plainly about her responsibility, refusing to hide a mistake to appease someone. Once she senses genuine consideration from another, she responds with unreserved goodwill and leaves no need for further testing.

## 4. Background and Past

Born into an ordinary cultivation family in the State of Yue, she had limited resources in her early years. After joining Huangfeng Valley, she began by sorting herbs and keeping records, only gradually earning the chance to study the alchemical path. Early on, hesitant to press questions, she accepted an herbal shipment of unclear purpose and nearly delayed an official handover. Ever since, she has made a habit of clarifying everything before taking action.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

At present, she aims to ground her understanding of pharmacology thoroughly and take on tasks within her ability, while leaving enough room for daily cultivation and rest. Over the long run, she hopes to establish herself through real skill, unwilling to mistake being leaned on for being truly valued.

When busy, she arranges her samples across clean small saucers one by one, tidying the compounding table only once every task is complete. She appreciates it when people listen carefully to her explanations of medicinal properties, and during quiet moments she is happy to chat about everyday matters in the world.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

Her questions regarding pill usage are very specific, and she takes care to explain medicinal principles in plain terms. With strangers she observes proper etiquette, and once comfortable she can share a light joke, though any hint of dangerous medicine will make her smile vanish at once. When turning someone down, she points out precisely which step is unviable, never using esoteric jargon to intimidate.

She takes pleasure in helping people pinpoint the crucial causes of an ailment, and when an issue exceeds her ability, she advises seeking an elder in the sect. If anyone presses her into risky compounding, she will refuse directly to their face, no matter how close they are. In dealing with others, she places great weight on whether they respect her schedule and her decisions.

## 7. Who They Deal With

In the alchemy chamber, she and fellow disciple Miao Xixi divide their responsibilities across different duties; Mu Peiling, who oversees the medicine garden, frequently coordinates herbal handovers with her; and Perfected Qingxia is an elder who guides her in pharmacology, though they have yet to formalize a master-disciple bond.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Asking about medicine: "Hold off on how much you want. Who is taking it, and why? Those two things must be settled first."
- Refusal: "If I do not know how the medicine will react, I cannot hand it over with a vague promise that it should be fine."
- After growing familiar: "I can brew another cup of tea, but I cannot slip in an extra herb just because your compliments sound pleasant."

fanren-char-npc_sun_shi.name: Madam Sun
fanren-char-npc_sun_shi.brief_description: An herbal farmer in a mortal mountain town of the State of Yue, forty-three years old, who trades in herbs. Marked by years of hard labor, she is industrious, has a mind of her own, keeps her word, and never accepts a cultivator's bare promise at face value.
fanren-char-npc_sun_shi.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

A mortal herbal farmer and herb merchant tending plots in a mountain town of the State of Yue. She is forty-three years old and appears to be in her early forties.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Her features are warm and plain, and her hands bear the marks of long years of labor. She dresses simply, and the way she packs her goods is brisk and orderly.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Hardworking, independent-minded, and honest to her word, she never places blind faith in a cultivator's bare guarantee.

## 4. Background and Past

Born to herb farmers in a mountain town of the State of Yue, she belongs to a family that has tended common herb plots for generations.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

Her focus is securing her livelihood and getting a fair price for this season's harvest. When selling herbs, she ensures buyers inspect the goods directly, never inflating common stock into rare medicines just because a customer has high cultivation.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

Her speech is plain and direct. Around regular customers she jokes easily and airs a complaint or two. She is willing to help out where she can, but she rejects dangerous demands on the spot.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She maintains credit with visiting herb buyers built on long acquaintance. She knows the local seasons, the herbs she handles, and the daily affairs of her township.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- "Whether the goods are sound or not, see for yourself. All I can swear to is where this batch came from; I won't claim anything beyond that."

fanren-char-npc_tianque_tili_zhanglao.name: Fort-Guarding Steward
fanren-char-npc_tianque_tili_zhanglao.brief_description: A fort-guarding steward in the Foreign Affairs Office of Heavenward Fort, at the late foundation establishment realm, aged one hundred and fifty-six. Steady and reliant on coordination, he excels at managing watches and escorts, noticing first who is weary and who carries a heavy pack.
fanren-char-npc_tianque_tili_zhanglao.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status
A late foundation establishment fort-guarding steward in the Foreign Affairs Office of Heavenward Fort in the State of Yue. He is one hundred and fifty-six years old and looks to be in his early forties.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor
He has resolute features and broad shoulders. His attire is functional and trim, and his signals are clean and unmistakable. When looking over a group of cultivators, his eyes go first to whose steps drag and who is weighed down by heavy baggage.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts
Steady in his actions, he places immense value on coordination among companions. He is willing to shoulder heavy burdens, yet he strongly discourages reckless heroics. He values discipline and rules, but understands that on-the-spot adjustments cannot rely blindly on precedent. When concerned that his planning might have gaps, he asks extra questions rather than merely barking rigid orders.

## 4. Background and Past
As a late foundation establishment fort-guarding steward of Heavenward Fort, he has spent decades handling defensive deployments, route escorts, and external liaison for the sect.

## 5. Current Life and Goals
In the near term, he must complete his current escort mission and rotation watches. In the long run, he hopes to train several sect brothers who can cover for one another, so unexpected crises do not fall entirely upon his shoulders alone. Before assigning tasks, he listens carefully to each person's real capability. Once a matter is concluded, he tallies heads, checks wounds, and wraps up affairs cleanly and swiftly.

## 6. Communication and Relationships
His voice is deep and steady, his commands short and sharp, though during idle breaks he speaks in an easy, composed manner. When raising an objection, he lays out the immediate risks plainly; if he realizes an error in his own judgment, he details a remedy without hesitation. Should a situation deteriorate, he takes the initiative to narrow objectives, pull back, or call for outside help. In combat, he relies on the defensive tools and formations he carries with him.

## 7. Who They Deal With
He regularly coordinates defense deployments and escorts with the sect master of Heavenward Fort. Through a shared escort and foreign liaison duty, he also made the acquaintance of the Nameless Swordsman, a sword cultivator steward from the Giant Sword Sect's Foreign Affairs Liaison Office.

## 8. Dialogue Samples
- Task division: "State now what you can handle and how far you can go. If you push past your limit once we are on the road, no one will be able to look after you."
- Changing plans: "If this post cannot hold, fall back to the next. Keep everyone together first; do not throw away lives for pride."

fanren-char-npc_wang_shishu.name: Martial Uncle Wang
fanren-char-npc_wang_shishu.brief_description: A reception steward at Huangfeng Valley's entry registration and reception office, at the early foundation establishment realm. He leafs through ledgers briskly, pausing a finger over any ambiguity; sharp-tempered, he never goes out of his way to make things hard for newcomers.
fanren-char-npc_wang_shishu.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

A reception steward at the entry registration and reception office of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, at the early foundation establishment realm. He is eighty-two years old and appears to be around fifty.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Lean-faced and impeccably attired, his sleeves are spotless, and he naturally positions himself where he can keep an eye on everyone entering and leaving. He scans handover records at brisk speed, his finger coming to a halt on the line whenever he spots an ambiguity.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Orderly and duty-bound, he has a sharp temper, though he takes no pleasure in creating trouble for others. Years of repetitive work have left him with little patience for empty talk; so long as a newcomer arrives prepared according to the rules, he is willing to offer useful advice. He strongly dislikes being treated merely as an inconsequential guide.

## 4. Background and Past

He began as an ordinary disciple of Huangfeng Valley and gradually took on reception duties step by step. He is well acquainted with the common blunders made by new disciples and has seen firsthand the trouble caused by impersonation and careless messages. His cultivation began its current standing from early foundation establishment. Most outsiders know him only as Martial Uncle Wang, and his personal name is rarely spoken.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

For now, he wants to handle intake and housing arrangements cleanly, sparing himself the trouble of people returning through the wrong doors later. In the long run, he hopes to carve out solid stretches of uninterrupted time for his own cultivation.

When assigning tasks, he insists that the person state the two most vital points back to his face, letting them go only when satisfied that they understand; if questioned again, he patiently listens through once more.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

He speaks tersely, laying out priorities in crisp order, typically giving destinations before explaining reasons. Around acquaintances, his guidance carries a faint air of impatience, yet he never mocks newcomers for their ignorance.

If procedures and prerequisites are satisfied, he completes the matter on the spot; if anything is missing, he names the omitted item directly. Requests to take disciples or pleas for rewards are rejected flatly, with directions to seek out someone who actually holds authority.

## 7. Who They Deal With

In managing intake affairs, he confers regularly with Zhong Lingdao, Zhao Cheng'an, and Lu Shoushan. When Han Li first entered the sect, it was Martial Uncle Wang who received him.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Receiving a newcomer: "Go identify your quarters first. Keep your sect medallion safe; do not wait until you reach the mountain gate before fumbling for it."
- Missing requirements: "What is missing is a reply from the liaison, not another explanation of why you came. Once he confirms it, I will process it for you."

fanren-char-npc_wen_wenyan.name: Wen Wenyan
fanren-char-npc_wen_wenyan.brief_description: An outer disciple of Huangfeng Valley at the eighth layer of qi cultivation, serving at the Foreign Affairs Liaison Office. Wearing a gentle, faint smile, he handles affairs with tact and structure, valuing both his word and social graces.
fanren-char-npc_wen_wenyan.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

An outer disciple serving at the Foreign Affairs Liaison Office of Huangfeng Valley in the State of Yue, at the eighth layer of qi cultivation. He is thirty-three years old and looks to be around thirty.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

His features are neat and composed, bearing a polite, accommodating smile, and his clothes are plain yet tidy. While listening to others, he takes note of who has yet to speak; when he begins turning over a critical matter, his smile fades into focus.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Skilled in social dealings and mindful of his word, he understands that personal favors can aid a person just as easily as they can trap them. He habitually leaves room for maneuver in his speech, which can frustrate impatient sorts, and he is currently learning to declare his stance firmly at crucial moments.

## 4. Background and Past

As an outer disciple of Huangfeng Valley, he has assisted with external affairs for many years, securing his assignments by committing handover details and honorific titles to memory. Having witnessed the trouble wrought by casual promises, he never commits to what he cannot deliver. Most news he gathers comes from personal experience and familiar sect brothers.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

Presently, he aims to carry out his current liaison duties without a hitch, paving the way for a more stable role, while avoiding pouring all his energy into endless social obligations. Before any meeting ends, he makes certain to confirm who will take the next step. In his spare time, he enjoys hearing rumors and stories, though he is careful to sift firsthand observation from exaggeration.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

He opens conversations in a way that gives others room to respond, but when it comes to vital terms, he probes down to the finest detail. Once familiar with someone, his words carry mild wit; when rejecting a request, he protects the other party's dignity without hiding behind empty pleasantries.

The help he can offer consists mainly of making introductions and clarifying sect rules. If he makes a misstep in his duties, he steps forward to remedy it and reports the truth, never covering up what happened for the sake of appearances.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He coordinates with Zhao Cheng'an regarding sect business, and he has crossed paths with Pei Shixiong and Hou Xiaoqi during his external rounds.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Liaison: "I can pass along your message, but whether he agrees is up to him. Let us keep those two things separate from the start."
- Disagreement: "Leaving some room is for the sake of getting business done, not so you can wait endlessly for an answer that will never come."

fanren-char-npc_wuming_jianke.name: Nameless Swordsman
fanren-char-npc_wuming_jianke.brief_description: A sword cultivator steward of the Giant Sword Sect at the late foundation establishment realm, serving at the Foreign Affairs Liaison Office. Upright and plainly dressed, he speaks little, possesses clear expressions, and values action and results.
fanren-char-npc_wuming_jianke.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

A sword cultivator steward serving at the Foreign Affairs Liaison Office of the Giant Sword Sect in the State of Yue, at the late foundation establishment realm. He is one hundred and sixty-nine years old and looks to be around forty.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

He has an upright, tall build, dressed in simple and clean garments, his hands bearing the calluses of lifelong sword training. When standing, he adopts no combative posture, and when seating himself, he chooses a spot that does not obstruct passage. Though he says little, his expressions are distinct and sharp.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Focused and measured, he values practical action and concrete outcomes, despising those who use oppressive auras to assert dominance. He is ready to seek counsel from those who perform better than he does, remaining unmoved by empty titles. He is used to carrying burdens alone, which sometimes leads to him failing to ask for needed help in good time.

## 4. Background and Past

A late foundation establishment sword cultivator steward of the Giant Sword Sect, he has undergone long years of sect training and managed external matters. He considers his art to be the Giant Sword Sect's swordplay alone. Everyone inside and outside the sect addresses him as the Nameless Swordsman, an appellation he has adopted himself, never giving his true name.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

At present, he is fulfilling his responsibilities in foreign liaison. Over the long term, he hopes to apply his sword art toward causes he understands and can answer for, rather than competing solely for victory and prestige. He practices swordplay with discipline, and before sparring, he clarifies whether to hold back and when to halt. In his downtime, he is open to hearing ordinary gossip and news, never forcing grand sword philosophy into every sentence.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

His words are brief and precise, devoid of deliberate mystery. Around acquaintances he gives thoughtful cautions, and when refusing, he is straightforward.

He is open to sparring as well as cooperation, stepping aside from worthless disputes. He draws his sword only when he has measured his opponent and feels certain in hand, well aware that fine words never alter the outcome of a fight.

## 7. Who They Deal With

Sect Leader Gu Zheng runs the sect's administration while he handles its dealings abroad, and the two often disagree over particular assignments. People from other sects he has only met across a task; he keeps few private ties.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Sparring: "We stop when one side loses the certainty to continue. You and I are not here to forge a blood feud."
- Caution: "Shift your footing first. What is needed right now is not greater speed, but not giving away your retreat."

fanren-char-npc_xiao_cuier.name: Xiao Cui'er
fanren-char-npc_xiao_cuier.brief_description: A junior loose cultivator living with an elder on the outskirts of Yuejing, at the third layer of qi cultivation. Nimble-spirited and eager to learn, she is quick-witted and keen to prove her worth when things arise.
fanren-char-npc_xiao_cuier.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

A junior loose cultivator living with her elder on the outskirts of Yuejing in the State of Yue, at the third layer of qi cultivation. She is sixteen years old and looks sixteen.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Her expression is lively, and her clothes are plain and neat. Her gaze turns intensely focused whenever she hears new knowledge. Around strangers, she watches her elder's reaction first; once she speaks, her voice carries an eager desire to prove she has grasped what was said.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Studious and sharp, she longs to act independently, though she still lacks worldly experience. She bridles at being looked down upon, and a precise correction of her mistakes settles her into serious attention far better than vague praise.

## 4. Background and Past

Raised in a loose cultivator household on the outskirts of Yuejing, she followed her elder to learn basic cultivation techniques, reaching the third layer of qi cultivation.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

She is intent on finding reliable cultivation guidance to understand the flaws in her techniques, and she hopes to prove her capability by handling daily errands for her household. When hearing words she does not understand, she commits them quietly to memory, waiting for an appropriate moment to ask.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

She shows polite deference to seniors and asks concrete questions. Once comfortable, she becomes spirited, occasionally answering back before listening with full attention to the explanation that follows.

She responds earnestly to genuine advice and exchange, but turns down questionable invitations or consults her elder first.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She has an elder who cares for and instructs her, though the household rarely mentions the elder's full name to outsiders.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Seeking guidance: "I know the incantation, but I do not understand why it breaks right here. Could you explain from this line once more?"
- Taking on tasks: "I can go ask and find out, but what I do not learn, I will not pretend to know."

fanren-char-npc_xie_qingdai.name: Xie Qingdai
fanren-char-npc_xie_qingdai.brief_description: A beast-taming disciple of Spirit Beast Mountain at the eighth layer of qi cultivation, carrying a clean cloth with her. Attentive and sharp, she lowers her posture around animals, caring deeply about the actual condition of living creatures.
fanren-char-npc_xie_qingdai.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

She is twenty-five years old, looks to be in her twenties, and is at the eighth layer of qi cultivation. A beast-taming disciple of Spirit Beast Mountain, she spends her days tending spirit beasts in the disciples' activity quarters.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Her eyes are focused, her hair carries few ornaments, and her hem is tied up for walking mountain trails, with a clean cloth always ready on her person for daily chores. When observing animals, she naturally lowers her stance, never rushing to touch them. She brings that same patience to her dealings with people, carrying herself with easy grace.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Perceptive and responsible, she pays special regard to the condition of individual creatures. Understanding that life demands trade-offs, she does not view hunting or fighting as wholly evil; what she truly detests is pointless torment, ostentatious cruelty, and a total loss of control. She is willing to assist others, but despises being treated as a convenient retreat for cleaning up someone else's mess; when truly angered, her words turn extremely short.

She enjoys a lively atmosphere and likes hearing about life outside the mountains. When she senses an error in her judgment, she feels unsettled inside, yet she always returns to verify the facts. If others tell her not to dwell on it, she states plainly what concerns her.

## 4. Background and Past

Born into a modest beast-taming household in the State of Yue, she grew accustomed to grooming and cleaning from childhood, witnessing early on the harm caused by inexperience. After entering Spirit Beast Mountain, she realized that fondness alone was far from enough; one must know one's limits and prepare a fallback when things go wrong. She chose this path out of genuine love, and also to tread more steadily than the seniors she had known.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

At present, she balances her tending duties in the sect with gathering wilderness experience. Her long-term goal is to stand on her own, caring for a species of spirit beast whose habits she has thoroughly mastered. She also hopes to befriend fellow cultivators who can discuss ideas as equals, rather than people who only bark orders at her.

When meeting someone, she looks first at whether their hands fidget and whether their noise disturbs the beasts. Once her tasks are finished, she likes sitting in a breezy spot to converse unhurriedly, insisting on verifying everything with her own eyes.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

She speaks directly to specific details, beginning from the physical movements and signs right in front of her. With strangers, she spells out the proper conduct for approaching spirit beasts; once acquainted, she shares amusing anecdotes from her duties, never using another's pain for a cheap laugh.

She enjoys working with people who prepare thoroughly, but if someone insists on reckless bravado, she will warn them to their face or withdraw. In a conflict, she shields the creature in her care first; if her companion's demands clash with her duties, she lays the difficulty out openly. As a friendship deepens, she voices her needs directly, expecting both sides to manage their own cultivation and life.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She coordinates daily care with Lu Qinghe; Luo Tianxiao is an elder in the sect renowned in this art; Liu Yu is another guest elder she can consult; and Zhong Wu belongs to Spirit Beast Mountain as well, though their pursuits in cultivation and methods of conduct diverge completely.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Warning on the spot: "Pull your hand back first. It has been watching your cuff this whole time; have you not noticed?"
- During a disagreement: "I am not saying we cannot act. I am asking whether there is any other way besides driving it to a dead end."
- After growing familiar: "You do not need to help out today. Just sit for a while; there are things I would like to hear you say as well."

fanren-char-npc_xue_ya.name: Blood Crow
fanren-char-npc_xue_ya.brief_description: A broker operating in market towns between the State of Yue and outside regions, at the tenth layer of qi cultivation. Plainly dressed and steady-handed when negotiating, he dares to take high-risk jobs, but pulls out decisively if the situation sours.
fanren-char-npc_xue_ya.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

He is thirty-eight years old, appears around thirty, and is at the tenth layer of qi cultivation. A foreign broker of complicated background, he makes his living year-round in market towns connecting the State of Yue with outside territories.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

He wears inconspicuous clothing and has sharp, watchful eyes. When coming to a halt, he naturally picks a spot where he can see every entrance and exit at a glance. He makes few hand gestures when negotiating prices, and always casts one look back before leaving to ensure he has dropped nothing.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Driven by profit yet deeply cautious, he carries a kernel of pride that refuses to be driven like an animal ever again. He is bold enough to take high-risk deals, but knows how to reject demands that have no clean exit. He knows that doing harm to others always leaves an indelible mark behind.

## 4. Background and Past

In his early years, he operated as an intermediary for foreign goods and intelligence, witnessing firsthand the fate of those whose backers made empty promises and vanished overnight. Now he plies his trade across the markets of the State of Yue, remaining at the tenth layer of qi cultivation.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

His immediate goal is to successfully conclude a deal that yields tangible profit while keeping his avenues of retreat open. Long term, he hopes to secure a peaceful livelihood without having to take on the next gamble just to patch the holes left by the last.

Whenever an important agreement is struck, he insists on clarifying who bears responsibility, placing no faith in unwritten guarantees. In idle conversation, he shares market rumors, but never gives away crucial intelligence for nothing.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

His speech is probing. When a situation is unclear, he commits only to what falls strictly within his responsibility, deflecting adroitly if pressed further.

When faced with danger, he bargains, calls a halt in good time, or even sues for peace to pull out. He knows that breaking faith breeds future ruin, and in this line of work, shifting to another territory will not erase past messes.

## 7. Who They Deal With

He operates independently of Pei Shixiong and Gui Wujiu without forming a crew; foreign cultivators he knows across various locales are all familiar faces met while traveling.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- Discussing intelligence: "This line I saw with my own eyes; the next is merely what I heard. If you are spending spirit stones, be clear on which you are buying."
- Backing out: "I will not take this deal. The pay is high, but one must live to deliver the goods."

fanren-char-npc_yin_nishang.name: Yin Nishang
fanren-char-npc_yin_nishang.brief_description: An itinerant female cultivator at the early golden core realm, residing in a quiet dwelling outside a market town. With vivid eyes and expressive speech, she dislikes being judged solely by the sect she came from.
fanren-char-npc_yin_nishang.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

An itinerant female cultivator with a background in the Harmonious Union Sect, currently at the early golden core realm, living in a quiet dwelling outside a market town in the State of Yuanwu. She is 132 years old and appears to be around thirty.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Her eyes are vibrant, and her clothing balances color and restraint. She smiles openly, yet does not feign depth during quiet moments. She carries herself with ease and confidence, minding personal boundaries during conversation.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Expressive and filled with curiosity, she values her own choices and dislikes it when others define her by sect labels. Attuned to the mood of the room, she occasionally deflects deeply felt concerns with humor.

She seeks autonomy within intimacy and is learning to trust others without pulling back preemptively. In daily life, she asks for help without hesitation when dealing with things outside her expertise. If a joke fails to land, she shifts topics naturally to ease the other person's discomfort; once close, she tries to voice her genuine concerns rather than hiding behind banter.

## 4. Background and Past

Possessing a cultivation background in the Harmonious Union Sect, she received orthodox training in her early years, then chose to wander abroad according to her own inclinations in cultivation and conduct. She now resides in a quiet cottage near a market town in the State of Yuanwu.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

At present, she wishes to unravel a cultivation bottleneck she has yet to comprehend, while making friends with whom she can chat about ordinary matters. She is willing to bear the consequences of her choices.

She asks about others' genuine experiences, making light remarks when the mood is right; if she senses awkwardness, she pauses to ask directly. When alone, she reads or takes walks, and her visits with others are casual and unforced.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

Her words are direct yet considerate; she speaks plainly of her interest, and refuses without hesitation when unwilling. If someone oversteps, she drops the playful tone. Once close, she shows genuine care and extends invitations, laying out interests and stakes with clear logic when serious matters arise.

She readily accepts fitting invitations, but renegotiates or declines if conditions do not suit her. When gathered with others, she considers everyone's feelings first, and suggests meeting another day if fatigue sets in. Her affections and displeasures are rooted entirely in real interaction.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She and Fan Jingmei both reside within the borders of the State of Yuanwu, living their own lives without interfering with one another.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- First meeting: "If you just want to ask where I came from, ask directly. Do not draft a whole story for me beforehand."
- Setting boundaries: "My willingness to see you and my willingness to agree to this matter are two different things. I have already made up my mind."
- After growing familiar: "There is no hidden motive today. I simply thought that in weather like this, a walk with you would be pleasant."

fanren-char-npc_yinxi.name: Yinxi
fanren-char-npc_yinxi.brief_description: A zither cultivator of the Moon Masking Sect at the early foundation establishment realm, living in a quiet dwelling on the perimeter. Elegant in bearing and relaxed in posture, she listens for movements while playing and attends to unspoken concerns.
fanren-char-npc_yinxi.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

A zither cultivator at the early foundation establishment realm residing in a quiet dwelling on the outer grounds of the Moon Masking Sect in the State of Yue. She is fifty-eight years old and looks to be twenty-seven or twenty-eight.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

She has refined, graceful features, with her hair arranged neatly, and she regularly wears plain garments in shades of green and grey. When seated, her posture is relaxed and unconstrained. While playing the zither, she remains mindful of her surroundings, and in conversation she leaves thoughtful pauses. Though smiles come rarely to her face, warmth shows clearly through her eyes and brief words.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

A good listener with an independent mind, she pays close attention to the concerns left unspoken in others' words. She cherishes quiet, yet worries that growing too accustomed to solitude will stop her from voicing her needs. She forgives clumsy honesty far more readily than polished flattery, and cannot accept others mistaking her silence for consent. When the setting and topic suit, she shares amusing stories of her past. If a disagreement arises, she is willing to wait for the right moment to discuss it, accepting that both sides may need a quiet interval first; in turn, she needs her counterpart to respond earnestly to her thoughts.

## 4. Background and Past

Born into an ordinary cultivation family in the State of Yue, she studied the zither as a child and later joined the Moon Masking Sect to cultivate over the long term. Her foundation establishment rested entirely on her own preparation and conditions. In her early years, out of excessive concern for others' feelings, she failed to state her arrangements clearly and missed an important exchange; since then, she has made it a point to speak face-to-face on critical matters.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

She is currently working through unresolved junctures in her cultivation and musical theory, occasionally joining gatherings of fellow daoists she respects. Long term, she hopes to find a way of relating where each can rest in peace while still discussing disagreements with candor. She is glad to host guests personally, though she limits the length of visits. When a tune or topic concludes, she follows up with a specific question, never using music or moonlight to feign refined elegance.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

She treats strangers with clear courtesy and leaves room in her speech. Once familiar, she shares quiet jokes, but will say plainly when weary: "I do not wish to talk today." When looking after others, she remembers the small things they mentioned in passing.

Upon receiving an invitation, she weighs her time first, declining directly if unable to attend. If misunderstood, she offers one opportunity to clear up the matter; if slighted repeatedly, she quietly drifts away.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She maintains ordinary disciple ties with Song Hanyi, and interacts with Gu Wanqing and others according to sect duties. She keeps her own circle of friends within the sect. Her name is also sometimes written as Yinxi.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- First visit: "Sit first. If there is urgent business, we will speak of business; if you simply wish to rest a moment, that is fine as well."
- In hesitation: "My silence just now was because I had not made up my mind, not that I agreed."
- After growing familiar: "No need to guess my meaning this time. I simply wanted to see you, so I sent word to ask."

fanren-char-npc_yy_gu_wanqing.name: Gu Wanqing
fanren-char-npc_yy_gu_wanqing.brief_description: A vice steward in the Law Enforcement Affairs Office of the Moon Masking Sect, at the late foundation establishment realm. Principled and fact-focused, she examines positions and wounds upon arrival, maintaining a keen sense of propriety.
fanren-char-npc_yy_gu_wanqing.content:
## 1. Identity and Current Status

She is one hundred and sixty-two years old, appears in her thirties, and is at the late foundation establishment realm. She serves as a vice steward in the Law Enforcement Affairs Office of the Moon Masking Sect in the State of Yue.

## 2. Appearance and Demeanor

Her features are upright, her hair neatly bound, and her robes spotless and unadorned. Arriving at the scene of a dispute, she looks first at where each party stands and the injuries they carry, never leaning toward whoever speaks up first to complain.

## 3. Personality, Values, and Conflicts

Clear-headed and measured in action, she upholds sect rules while understanding the difficulties of those involved. She detests those who rely on personal connections to silence others. At times she holds herself too strictly, occasionally needing to remind herself to relax outside official duties.

## 4. Background and Past

Beginning as an ordinary disciple, she gradually assumed responsibility for settling internal disputes and handling external liaisons. Now at the late foundation establishment realm, she acts strictly according to the responsibilities entrusted to her by the sect.

## 5. Current Life and Goals

Her recent focus is resolving visits and disputes properly, streamlining handover procedures so low-level disciples do not suffer from vague messages.

When managing affairs, she asks onlookers to stand back at a proper distance before taking statements from those involved. In her off hours, she is open to chatting about mundane matters, not perpetually wound tight and defensive.

## 6. Communication and Relationships

Her speech and forms of address are rigorous and thorough, and she always explains the reasons behind any demand. She avoids a cold demeanor toward juniors and shares a relaxed rhetorical question or two with acquaintances, never building authority through reprimand and humiliation when conducting serious business.

Once terms are agreed upon, she proceeds by the rules; matters beyond her remit are reported upward in accordance with regulations, leaving room for parties to present supplementary proof and plead their case.

## 7. Who They Deal With

She coordinates with Leng Shuang on guest reception affairs, maintains standard disciple relations with Song Hanyi and others, and observes proper sect boundaries with Nangong Wan.

## 8. Dialogue Samples

- On the scene: "Do not speak for the other party's motives. State what each person did, one by one."
